classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Local toroidal component of the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity at the
plasma boundary, density-weighted over all hydrogen charge states.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity component tangent
to the toroidal direction at the plasma boundary, rather than a flux-surface
average. Hydrogen denotes the combined hydrogen-ion population.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{phi,H}(R,Z)=\mathbf{v}_H(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\phi},\qquad \mathbf{v}_H=\frac{\sum_q n_{H,q}\mathbf{v}_{H,q}}{\sum_q n_{H,q}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_H$ is the hydrogen bulk-flow velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the
toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
$n_{H,q}$ is the density of hydrogen charge state $q$, and
$\mathbf{v}_{H,q}$ is its bulk-flow velocity. The coordinates $R$ and $Z$
are major radius and vertical height, respectively. The local quantity is
distinct from the toroidal flux-surface-averaged hydrogen velocity at the
plasma boundary.

items.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Signed component along the y axis of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position, in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed y projection of the unit vector defining an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror’s translation direction or rotation axis
at its home position.

Let $d_y$ denote this component, $chat{\mathbf d}$ the defining unit
direction vector, and $chat{\mathbf y}$ the unit vector along the positive y
axis of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis:

$$
d_y = \hat{\mathbf d} \cdot \hat{\mathbf y}
$$

The corresponding [x-axis
component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
and [z-axis
component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror)
complete the Cartesian components of the same unit vector. This quantity
describes direction, not the mirror’s position or displacement.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Signed poloidal projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid
velocity for one ion charge state, distinct from individual guiding-center
motion and total poloidal flow.
items.documentation:
The poloidal ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge
state. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the
guiding-center motion of individual ions and is not restricted to the plasma
edge.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,\mathrm{p}} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal diamagnetic-drift velocity
component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla
p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field
vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle
charge, and $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is tangent to the local poloidal contour
toward increasing specified poloidal angle $\theta$. It lies in a
constant-toroidal-angle plane of the right-handed cylindrical frame
$(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The orientation of $\theta$ must
be specified independently of the magnetic-field direction.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow. It is the diamagnetic contribution to the [poloidal ion
charge-state velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_velocity), not the
total poloidal flow. Although the diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular
to the magnetic field, its geometric poloidal component need not vanish.

For a species-level velocity, the diamagnetic contribution is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, not their sum.
Projecting that mean onto the local binormal direction gives the sibling
[binormal ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which differs
from this quantity in both projection and charge-state aggregation.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified
ion charge state has a component toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$
in a constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame.

items.name: neutral_velocity
items.description:
Mean translational velocity of a neutral-particle population, resolved or
averaged over internal states and energy ranges, with component projections
representing the same bulk flow.
items.documentation:
The neutral velocity is the mean translational flow of a selected
neutral-particle population, whether resolved by internal state or energy
range or aggregated over several such populations.

At position $\mathbf r$, it is defined by the first velocity moment:

$$
\mathbf{u}_n(\mathbf r)=\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int \mathbf v\,f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{n,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $\mathbf r$ is position in m, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity in m
s$^{-1}$, $f_{n,a}$ is phase-space density in m$^{-6}$ s$^3$, $a$ labels
included internal-state or energy subpopulations, and $\mathcal A$ is the
included set. A resolved form is represented by [neutral internal-state
velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity), while aggregation over
included states gives a bulk form such as [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). Vertical, poloidal,
parallel, cold, and hot variants select projections or population subsets of
this same mean flow.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode_center
items.description:
Toroidal flux coordinate at the neoclassical tearing mode center, a
non-negative, radius-like magnetic-surface label derived from enclosed
toroidal magnetic flux.
items.documentation:
Toroidal flux coordinate

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor}} = \sqrt{\Phi/(\pi B_0)}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate at the mode
center, $\Phi$ is the magnitude of the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by
the associated surface, and $B_0$ is the positive vacuum toroidal
magnetic-field strength at the reference major radius.

This quantity is the [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate) evaluated at the stated locus,
not a geometric major radius or a distance from the magnetic axis. It is
dimensional rather than normalized; its normalized counterpart is obtained
by dividing it by the [toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: argon_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Charge-state-summed local number density of argon ions at the H-mode edge
pedestal top, excluding neutral argon.
items.documentation:
The local argon-ion number density at the H-mode edge pedestal top is the
physical count of argon ions per plasma volume at that locus, aggregated
across ionization states. It excludes neutral argon and is neither
chord-averaged nor volume-averaged.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{z=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total local argon-ion number density, $z$ is
the positive integer argon charge state, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{z+}}$ is the
local number density of argon ions in charge state $z$. The sum includes Ar+
through Ar18+.

The quantity is evaluated at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, whose
location is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is a
locus-specific form of [argon density](name:argon_density), whereas
[line-averaged argon density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) represents
averaging along a plasma path rather than a local value.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Field-aligned projection of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion charge
state in the edge plasma, identically zero for the ideal drift.
items.documentation:
The parallel component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
projection along the local magnetic-field direction. For the ideal E×B
drift, this component vanishes identically.

For the ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2} = 0.
$$

Here $v_{E,\parallel}$ is the parallel drift component for the specified ion
charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its ideal E×B guiding-center drift velocity,
$\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic
field, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector
along the magnetic field. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field
and applies to magnetized ions.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge
states or species. It includes only the E×B drift contribution, not the
total field-aligned ion flow, which may be nonzero. Other contributions to
ion motion are excluded.

The zero parallel projection follows from the perpendicularity of the ideal
E×B drift to the magnetic field. Other projections, such as the [toroidal
component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
need not vanish because their projection directions are not generally
field-aligned.

items.name: normalized_minor_radius_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Dimensionless minor-radius label of a magnetic flux surface, obtained by
normalizing its major-radius half-width to a specified positive reference
length.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the dimensionless minor-radius label assigned to a magnetic
flux surface from its radial extent in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{minor}} = \frac{R_{\max}-R_{\min}}{2L_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $R_{\max}$ and $R_{\min}$ are the maximum and minimum major-radius
coordinates of the surface, each in m, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the
specified positive reference length in m.

The label is a geometric normalization of the surface half-width; it is not
a magnetic-flux normalization and therefore is distinct from the [normalized
toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). Its
numerical value depends on the chosen reference length.

items.name: vertical_outline_of_divertor_tile
items.description:
Vertical outline of divertor tile is the signed vertical coordinate of each
contour point on the surface outline defining the geometric boundary of an
individual divertor tile in the poloidal cross-section.
items.documentation:
Vertical outline of divertor tile is the signed $Z$ coordinate of each
contour point on the surface outline defining the geometric boundary of an
individual divertor tile. The coordinate is expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies pointwise to the contour points of the tile surface
boundary in the poloidal cross-section spanned by $R$ and $Z$ at fixed
$\phi$. It is not a tile-center position, a surface normal, a full surface
description, or an aggregate over the tile; no averaging, summing, or
extrema over contour points are implied.

Together with the [radial outline of divertor
tile](name:radial_outline_of_divertor_tile), it specifies the poloidal
contour of the divertor-tile surface boundary. The radial partner gives the
corresponding $R$ coordinate for the same contour points, while this
quantity gives only their $Z$ coordinate.

Sign convention: Positive when the contour point is displaced in the
$+\hat{Z}$ direction from the origin of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: lower_wavelength_of_filter
items.description:
Lower wavelength of a filter is the vacuum spectral coordinate marking the
short-wavelength, high-photon-energy boundary of its transmitted passband.
items.documentation:
Wavelength of filter

The corresponding frequency and photon-energy boundaries satisfy:

$$
\lambda_L = \frac{c}{\nu_U} = \frac{hc}{E_U}
$$

where $\lambda_L$ is the lower vacuum [wavelength] bound, $c$ is the speed
of light in vacuum, $\nu_U$ is the upper frequency bound, $h$ is Planck's
constant, and $E_U$ is the upper photon-energy bound.

This is the lower-edge specialization of [wavelength of a
filter](name:wavelength_of_filter), not its nominal passband center or
passband width. Together with the [upper wavelength of the
filter](name:upper_wavelength_of_filter), it delimits the specified
transmission interval in vacuum wavelength. It does not denote the
wavelength within the filter material or specify the detailed transmission
curve.

items.name: reference_frequency_of_wave_beam
items.description:
Reference temporal carrier frequency of a probing electromagnetic wave beam,
specified before frequency conversion or modulation and used as the
phase-measurement baseline.
items.documentation:
The reference frequency of a probing electromagnetic wave beam is its main
temporal carrier frequency before frequency upshifting or modulation. It
establishes the baseline wave frequency for phase changes caused by plasma
refraction, including electron-density-dependent propagation.

The carrier frequency is related to the wave's angular frequency by:

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is the carrier frequency and $\omega$ is the angular frequency
describing temporal phase evolution.

This quantity denotes the beam's main reference frequency, not a
subsequently upshifted or modulated frequency, a received frequency, or a
local-oscillator frequency. The associated phase quantity is the [wave phase
of a wave beam](name:wave_phase_of_wave_beam), while [launched wave
duration](name:launched_wave_duration) describes the temporal extent of a
sweep rather than its carrier frequency.

items.name: parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged stress along the magnetic field carried by
suprathermal particles whose untrapped orbits follow the plasma-current
direction, including directed motion.
items.documentation:
The parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned kinetic
stress of suprathermal particles, averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
Co-passing particles occupy untrapped guiding-center orbits whose
orbit-averaged toroidal motion follows the plasma current.

In the nonrelativistic kinetic description, this component is defined by the
parallel second velocity moment:

$$
p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}(S) = \left\langle m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_S
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged
parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure of species $s$, $S$ is the
magnetic flux surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_S$ denotes its
volume-weighted thin-shell average. Here $m_s$ is the particle mass,
$f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing suprathermal portion
of the species distribution function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$
is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
parallel velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b}$, where
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity applies to the fast population of the represented species, not
a total over all fast-ion species. Multiple fast-particle distribution
contributions for that species add linearly. The velocity moment is not
centered on the population's mean velocity, so directed parallel motion
contributes. Thermal particles, trapped particles, counter-passing
particles, and transverse stress are excluded.

It is the co-passing orbit-class contribution to the [parallel fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure). Its relationship to the
[co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure)
is $\langle
p_s^{\mathrm{co,fast}}\rangle_S=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}})/3$,
where $p_s^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the local kinetic trace pressure and
$p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged transverse
stress per perpendicular degree of freedom for the same species and orbit
class. Thus the parallel component is not the isotropic trace pressure.

items.name: product_of_poloidal_current_function_and_derivative_of_poloidal_current_function_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate
items.description:
Grad–Shafranov equilibrium source term formed by multiplying the poloidal
current function by its derivative with respect to signed poloidal magnetic
flux.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface-dependent product of the poloidal current
function and its derivative with respect to the signed poloidal
magnetic-flux coordinate. It represents the toroidal-field contribution to
the Grad–Shafranov equilibrium source term.

The defining relation is

$$
G(\psi)=F(\psi)\frac{dF(\psi)}{d\psi}
$$

where $G(\psi)$ denotes this quantity, $F(\psi)$ is the [poloidal current
function](name:poloidal_current_function), $\psi$ is the signed poloidal
magnetic-flux coordinate, and $dF/d\psi$ is the derivative of that current
function with respect to $\psi$. The function $F$ is defined by $F=R
B_\phi$, where $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame and $B_\phi$ is the toroidal magnetic-field component.

This quantity applies to an axisymmetric equilibrium description on nested
magnetic flux surfaces. It is a local flux-function value with no additional
spatial averaging, species summation, or volume integration. It is distinct
from the poloidal current function itself and from its derivative alone.

Within the Grad–Shafranov balance, this product combines the toroidal-field
contribution with the pressure-gradient contribution to determine the
equilibrium relation for toroidal current density and force balance.

Sign convention: Positive when $F$ and $dF/d\psi$ have the same sign for the
chosen orientation of the signed poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate
items.description:
Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the
counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles
whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current
direction.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged
volumetric rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the
counter-passing orbit class. Counter-passing particles are passing particles
whose guiding-center toroidal circulation is opposite to the plasma-current
direction.

The source contribution to the evolution of the counter-passing thermal
particle number density is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)=\left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi,t)}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{source}}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is this source rate,
$n_{\mathrm{cp}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged number density
of counter-passing thermal particles, $\psi$ is the magnetic flux-surface
label, $t$ is time, and the source subscript denotes the explicit
particle-source contribution. Positive values represent net particle
addition, while negative values represent net particle removal.

This quantity applies only to the thermal population in the counter-passing
orbit class and is averaged over magnetic flux surfaces. It is not summed
over co-passing or trapped orbit classes and excludes nonthermal particle
populations. The corresponding [co-passing thermal particle source
rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) applies the same source
definition to the co-passing orbit class.

The broader [thermal particle source
rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate) aggregates the orbit-population
contributions, including this counter-passing component; this quantity
therefore represents only the counter-passing contribution rather than the
total thermal source.

items.name: gap_at_outboard_midplane
items.description:
Gap at the outboard midplane is the major-radius separation between the
inner and outer separatrices in a double-null or near-double-null
equilibrium.
items.documentation:
Gap at outboard midplane

The separation is defined by

$$
g = \left|R_{\mathrm{outer}}-R_{\mathrm{inner}}\right|
$$

where $g$ is the gap, and $R_{\mathrm{outer}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{inner}}$ are
the major-radius coordinates of the outer and inner separatrices. Both
coordinates are evaluated at the same vertical height, selected by the inner
separatrix's outboard-midplane point. In the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ denotes major radius, $\phi$ toroidal angle, and $Z$
vertical height.

The quantity is a local separation, not a spatial average or a minimum
distance over the separatrix surfaces. It is nonnegative and vanishes when
the two separatrices coincide at the evaluation point.

Unlike [gap at closest wall point](name:gap_at_closest_wall_point), this
quantity compares two magnetic separatrices rather than a plasma boundary
and a material surface. It also differs from [radial separatrix distance at
outboard midplane](name:radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_midplane),
which compares a measurement position mapped along its flux surface with a
separatrix.

The low-field-side equatorial midplane: the point of maximum major radius on
the flux surface in question. For a value at the separatrix intersection use
outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $R = \max_{S} R,\quad R >
R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $S$ is the magnetic flux surface the point lies on;
$R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

items.name: total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall
items.description:
Thermal power extracted by active coolant circuits from cooled plasma-facing
wall surfaces, representing energy removal from the wall rather than
incident plasma power.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total heat-transfer rate from cooled plasma-facing wall
structures into their active coolant circuits. It represents energy removed
from the wall and is distinct from [total incident power at the
wall](name:total_incident_power_at_wall), which measures plasma power
arriving at wall surfaces.

$$
P_{\mathrm{cool}} = \sum_i \dot{Q}_{i}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cool}}$ is the total coolant-absorbed thermal power and
$\dot{Q}_{i}$ is the heat-transfer rate from the wall into coolant circuit
$i$. The sum includes all active cooling circuits serving the cooled
plasma-facing surfaces and excludes heat deposited on uncooled structures or
power merely incident on the wall.

items.name: momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of bulk-flow momentum.
This generic parent does not specify the transported plasma or neutral
population.
items.documentation:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of bulk-flow momentum.
This generic parent does not specify the transported plasma or neutral
population; population-qualified standard names identify that population.
Each component is a kinematic diagonal coefficient for one named transport
direction, not a full viscosity tensor.

For component $\chi_{m,i}$ associated with coordinate $x_i$ along direction
$\hat{e}_i$, the diagonal diffusive closure for momentum-density component
$M_j$ is

$$
\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{m,i}\,\frac{\partial M_j}{\partial x_i}\qquad\text{(no summation over }i\text{)}
$$

where $\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux in direction
$\hat{e}_i$ of momentum component $j$, $\chi_{m,i}$ is the directional
momentum diffusion coefficient, $M_j$ is the bulk-flow momentum density
component of the same transported population, and $x_i$ is distance along
$\hat{e}_i$.

The component basis must be explicit. A radial component is the $\hat{R}$
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from
the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed
from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is
the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel,
perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are
separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward
increasing flux label.

Population-qualified specializations include plasma momentum diffusion
coefficient, [ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and [neutral momentum
diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). Scalar
specializations include radial momentum diffusivity and ion momentum
diffusivity. This name is the momentum-channel specialization of diffusion
coefficient, and excludes convective momentum transport, external momentum
sources, off-diagonal couplings between flux and gradient directions, and
the dynamic viscosity-like coefficient obtained by multiplying by mass
density.

Sign convention: Positive when the diffusive momentum flux is directed
opposite to the corresponding gradient of bulk-flow momentum density.

items.name: tilt_angle_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Signed beta inclination of the beta-angle side of a plasma-filament
parallelogram cross-section in the poloidal plane of the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured counterclockwise from +Z toward
decreasing R.
items.documentation:
The tilt angle of a plasma filament is the signed inclination $\beta$ of the
beta-angle side of a plasma-filament parallelogram cross-section. The angle
lies in the poloidal $(R,Z)$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height,
and is referenced to the upward $+Z$ direction.

For the ordered parallelogram, let $\mathbf{u}_\beta =
u_R\hat{R}+u_Z\hat{Z}$ be the unit vector along the beta-angle side,
directed from the reference vertex shared with the base side toward the
adjacent beta-side vertex. The signed angle is defined by:

$$
\beta = \operatorname{atan2}(-u_R, u_Z)
$$

where $u_R$ and $u_Z$ are the components of $\mathbf{u}_\beta$ along
$\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$, and $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ returns the
principal branch $-\pi < \beta \le \pi$.

The beta-angle side terminology follows the same angle-labeled parallelogram
convention as [length of iron-core
segment](name:minor_length_of_iron_core_segment), identifying a side by its
inclination angle rather than by an ordinal label. The directed-edge and
branch conventions make $\beta$ unique: translating to the opposite parallel
edge leaves the value unchanged, while reversing the side direction is
excluded. This angle complements cross-section size quantities such as
[plasma-filament width](name:plasma_filament_width) and thickness of plasma
filament; it is not a filament-current direction or a magnetic-field pitch
angle.

Sign convention: Positive when the directed beta-angle side is rotated
counterclockwise from the upward $+Z$ direction in the poloidal $(R,Z)$
plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, drawn with $R$
increasing to the right.

items.name: vertical_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid
items.description:
Signed vertical component of the magnetic-field vector at a ferritic
element’s centroid in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical magnetic field at a ferritic element’s geometric centroid is
the projection of the local magnetic-field vector onto the vertical
direction. The centroid location is identified by the [vertical coordinate
of the ferritic element
centroid](name:z_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid), while this
quantity describes the field component there, not the element’s
magnetization.

$$
B_Z(\mathbf r_c)=\mathbf B(\mathbf r_c)\cdot\hat{\mathbf Z}
$$

where $\mathbf r_c$ is the centroid position, $\mathbf B$ is the local
magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf Z}$ is the vertical unit vector in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The radial, vertical, and
toroidal components together describe the local field; the corresponding
radial and toroidal quantities are [radial magnetic field at ferritic
element centroid](name:radial_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid)
and [toroidal magnetic field at ferritic element
centroid](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid).

Sign convention: Positive when $B_Z$ points in the direction of increasing
vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: beryllium_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Beryllium ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to
a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all beryllium ionization states
from Be1+ through Be4+.
items.documentation:
Beryllium density at a limiter is the local number density of beryllium ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath
or sheath entrance, where open scrape-off-layer field lines terminate on the
material surface. Unless a specific ionization stage is resolved, this
quantity is summed over all charged beryllium states; neutral beryllium
atoms are excluded.

The charge-state-summed density is defined as:

$$
n_\mathrm{Be} = \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in
ionization state $z$, spanning all four stages accessible under edge-plasma
conditions.

Beryllium is used as a plasma-facing material in several tokamak devices;
sputtering of beryllium limiter surfaces introduces impurity ions into the
scrape-off layer, where they contribute to fuel dilution and raise the
effective charge $Z_\mathrm{eff}$. This limiter-edge density sets the
impurity source boundary condition in edge transport models and is inferred
from spectroscopic line-emission measurements of beryllium charge states
combined with sheath or presheath models, or computed self-consistently in
coupled plasma-fluid and impurity-continuity solvers.

This quantity is the limiter-surface analog of
[beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary)
at the last-closed flux surface and of
[beryllium_density_at_divertor_target](name:beryllium_density_at_divertor_target)
at the divertor target. The parent
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) defines the evaluation locus
shared by all species-resolved limiter density quantities, including the
fuel-ion member
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter). The
volumetric profile away from the limiter is given by
[beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density).

items.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket
items.description:
Total rate of heat generation in all breeder-blanket materials from neutron
and photon interactions, excluding plasma-facing surface heat loads and
external incident power.
items.documentation:
Nuclear heating power of the breeder blanket is the total rate at which
neutron and photon interactions deposit energy as heat throughout all
included blanket materials. It is the blanket-wide nuclear component of
heating power of the breeder blanket.

The defining relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{BB}}} q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local nuclear heating power
density in W m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position within the blanket, $dV$ is
differential volume in m$^3$, and $V_{\mathrm{BB}}$ is the union of the
included blanket-module and constituent-material volumes.

The integral includes energy deposited by neutron scattering, neutron
capture, and photon interactions, including secondary gamma absorption,
without double-counting overlapping material descriptions. It excludes power
carried by neutrons or photons crossing into the blanket before deposition
and separate plasma-facing surface loads. Module- and layer-restricted
integrals are represented by [nuclear heating power of the breeder blanket
module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) and [nuclear
heating power of the breeder blanket
layer](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer), respectively.

items.name: toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Toroidal component of the volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer to
bulk thermal electrons through Coulomb collisions with other plasma species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque transferred to the
bulk thermal electron population by Coulomb collisions. It is the toroidal
projection of the volume-integrated thermal electron collisional torque,
including contributions from all specified collisional partners and
excluding noncollisional momentum transfer.

The volume-integrated torque is defined from the local [toroidal thermal
electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \tau_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal collisional
torque on thermal electrons, $\tau_{\phi,e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
corresponding local torque density, and $V$ is the integration volume. The
toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

Sign convention: Positive when collisional angular momentum is transferred
to the thermal electrons in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$.

items.name: accumulated_deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of deuterium delivered by gas
injection after plasma breakdown.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of deuterium atoms
delivered through gas injection, expressed using an equivalent-electron
weighting. It represents delivered fuel inventory rather than an
instantaneous injection rate or the number of electrons currently present in
the plasma.

The equivalent-electron convention is defined by

$$
N_D^{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_D N_D
$$

where $N_D^{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron inventory, $Z_D$ is the
atomic number of deuterium and equals one, and $N_D$ is the cumulative
number of deuterium atoms delivered after plasma breakdown.

The scope is restricted to deuterium introduced after plasma breakdown by
gas injection. Contributions are accumulated over the injection history and
weighted per deuterium atom; prefill delivery and other injected species are
excluded. Ionization after delivery does not change the assigned
equivalent-electron weighting.

The weighting convention is shared by
[accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection)
and
[accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection),
while this quantity remains specific to deuterium.

items.name: thermal_neutral_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of a neutral species arising from random thermal motion about its
mean flow, excluding nonthermal particles and directed-flow stress.
items.documentation:
Pressure of a neutral species is the isotropic part of its thermal kinetic
stress, arising from random translational motion about the mean flow. It is
one-third of the thermal pressure-tensor trace, rather than a selected
field-parallel or field-perpendicular component.

The defining central velocity moment is

$$
p_{0,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{m_0}{3}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_0|^2 f_0^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{0,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal neutral pressure, $m_0$ is the
neutral-particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_0$ is
the mean velocity of the thermal neutral population, $f_0^{\mathrm{th}}$ is
its velocity distribution normalized to its number density, and $d^3v$ is
the velocity-space volume element. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral
species. This trace definition does not require equal directional stresses.

The quantity applies to a specified neutral species, not a sum over
different neutral species. Thermal pressures are summed over all charge
states when multiple charge states are considered, rather than
density-weighted; for an exclusively neutral population, only the
zero-charge state contributes. Unlike [thermal neutral internal-state
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this species-level
quantity is not restricted to one specified internal state.

This is the thermal contribution to [total neutral
pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure). It excludes nonthermal
neutral-particle contributions and the momentum flux associated with mean
directed motion; subtracting the mean velocity in the defining moment
removes that directed-flow contribution.

items.name: total_plasma_radiated_power
items.description:
Total plasma radiated power is the electromagnetic energy emitted per unit
time by all plasma species, integrated over the entire emitting volume and
full photon spectrum.
items.documentation:
Total plasma radiated power is the rate at which the plasma emits energy as
electromagnetic radiation, integrated over the entire emitting plasma
volume.

$$
P_{\rm rad} = \int_{V_{\rm plasma}} \epsilon_{\rm rad}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\rm rad}$ is total plasma radiated power, $V_{\rm plasma}$ is the
emitting plasma volume, $\epsilon_{\rm rad}$ is the local electromagnetic
power emitted per unit volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$ is
a volume element. The emissivity includes all emitting species and charge
states, summed over all electromagnetic emission processes and integrated
over photon frequency and emission direction.

This quantity describes whole-plasma emission, not the radiation intercepted
by an individual detector or absorbed at a receiving surface. It excludes
conductive and convective energy losses and energy carried away by neutrons
or charged particles.

The [bremsstrahlung power](name:bremsstrahlung_power) and [power due to line
radiation](name:power_due_to_line_radiation) are mechanism-specific
contributions to this total, which also includes recombination and other
electromagnetic emission channels. The [radiated power over the core
region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region) is a regional contribution
rather than the whole-plasma aggregate.

items.name: parallel_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of suprathermal ions of one species and charge state arising from
velocity fluctuations along the local magnetic field, with the population's
mean flow removed.
items.documentation:
Pressure of suprathermal ions of one specified species and charge state is
the field-aligned normal stress from velocity fluctuations about that
population's mean flow. It is one of the two independent components of the
gyrotropic fast-ion pressure tensor, the other being perpendicular to the
local magnetic field.

The parallel pressure is defined by the field-aligned central second moment
of the fast-ion distribution:

$$
p_{s,c,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = m_s \int \left((\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right)^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{s,c,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-ion pressure
for species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position,
$m_s$ is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$
is the mean velocity of that fast-ion population, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$
is its velocity distribution function, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
volume element. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$
follows the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity includes only the specified suprathermal ion species and
charge state, with no sum over species or charge states. It excludes
thermal-ion and electron pressures, the perpendicular pressure component,
and stress from the population's mean directed motion. It is not the
isotropic trace pressure and does not require an isotropic distribution.

It is the parallel component of [fast-ion charge-state
pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure). Adding the contributions
from all charge states of a fixed ion species gives its [parallel fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_pressure); this aggregation is an additive
sum, not a density-weighted mean.

items.name: reference_magnetic_field
items.description:
Reference magnetic-field vector of the equilibrium magnetic induction
evaluated at the reference point, retaining field strength and direction
before selecting a component such as the toroidal reference magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The reference magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}$ is the equilibrium
[magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) evaluated at the reference point
used to define a local field reference. It represents the vector field at
that locus, retaining both field strength and direction rather than
selecting a cylindrical component or scalar magnitude.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the reference field may
be resolved as

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}=B_{R,{\rm ref}}\hat{R}+B_{\phi,{\rm ref}}\hat{\phi}+B_{Z,{\rm ref}}\hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_{\rm ref}$ is the reference magnetic field, $B_{R,{\rm
ref}}$ is its signed radial component, $B_{\phi,{\rm ref}}$ is the [toroidal
reference magnetic field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field),
$B_{Z,{\rm ref}}$ is its signed vertical component, and $\hat{R}$,
$\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ are the basis vectors for increasing major
radius, toroidal angle, and vertical height.

This quantity is defined at the reference point for the equilibrium field;
it is not the spatially unrestricted local [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field). It has no species population, and its
aggregation convention is a point value at the reference locus, not a
spatial average or finite-volume reduction.

The parent quantity is distinct from component-resolved reference fields:
the [toroidal reference magnetic
field](name:toroidal_reference_magnetic_field) is its projection along
$\hat{\phi}$ at the reference point, not a separate vector field. It is also
distinct from the unrestricted [toroidal magnetic
field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), which does not by name impose the
reference locus.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{B}_{\rm
ref}$ points along the corresponding positive basis vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where the positive directions
are increasing major radius $R$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and
increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: upper_bound_wavelength_of_visible_camera
items.description:
Long-wavelength boundary of the spectral sensitivity band accepted by a
visible-camera detector channel for photon detection.
items.documentation:
The upper-bound wavelength is the long-wavelength edge of the spectral
sensitivity band for a visible-camera detector channel. It identifies the
greatest wavelength included in the channel’s accepted photon-response
range.

The accepted wavelength interval is bounded by

$$
\lambda_{\mathrm{lower}} \leq \lambda \leq \lambda_{\mathrm{upper}}
$$

where $\lambda$ is photon wavelength, $\lambda_{\mathrm{lower}}$ is the
short-wavelength boundary given by [lower-bound wavelength of a visible
camera](name:lower_bound_wavelength_of_visible_camera), and
$\lambda_{\mathrm{upper}}$ is this quantity.

This is one boundary value for a visible-camera detector channel, not an
average wavelength, a band-integrated quantity, or the representative
wavelength assigned to an individual detector pixel. The paired lower and
upper boundaries delimit the channel’s spectral sensitivity band;
[wavelength of a detector pixel](name:wavelength_of_detector_pixel) instead
identifies a pixel-associated spectral coordinate.

items.name: x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Cartesian x-component of the unit vector directed along the major geometric
axis of the elliptic shatter cone.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the projection of the shatter cone’s major-axis unit vector
onto the Cartesian x direction. The major-axis unit vector specifies the
orientation of the elliptic shatter cone.

In the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, the
component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{major},x} = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}} \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}}$ is the unit vector along the
cone’s major axis, $\hat{x}$ is the Cartesian x-direction unit vector, and
$u_{\mathrm{major},x}$ is their scalar projection. The component
participates in the unit-vector constraint with the corresponding y and z
components. The [y major-axis unit-vector
component](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) resolves the same
axis in the y direction, whereas the [x minor-axis unit-vector
component](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) describes the
orthogonal minor axis.

items.name: efficiency_of_plant_system
items.description:
Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system converts
input power or energy into a specified useful output, abstracting over
thermal and net efficiency definitions.
items.documentation:
The efficiency of a plant system is a dimensionless performance metric
expressing the fraction of input power or energy that the plant converts
into a specified useful output. The exact physical scope depends on the
efficiency type applied: [thermal
efficiency](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system) characterizes
heat-to-work conversion across all thermodynamic conversion stages, while
[net efficiency](name:net_efficiency_of_plant_system) accounts for the
signed ratio of exported electrical power to total plant electrical
consumption including recirculating power.

The general defining relation takes the form:

$$
\eta = \frac{W_\text{out}}{W_\text{in}}
$$

where $W_\text{out}$ is the useful output (work, exported electrical power,
or heat converted to work) and $W_\text{in}$ is the total input power or
energy over the same operating interval.

Efficiency is evaluated from calorimetric heat-flow surveys, electrical
generation meters, and auxiliary power consumption measurements across all
plant subsystems. For fusion facilities, thermal conversion efficiencies in
steam-cycle plants lie in the range 30–45%, and net electrical efficiencies
are further reduced by recirculating power fractions for heating, current
drive, and cooling systems.

items.name: xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all xenon ionization states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the xenon ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local xenon-ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents xenon ions specifically, rather than neutral xenon,
electrons, or another ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe,axis}}$ is the xenon-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the number of xenon ions summed over all xenon
ionization states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete xenon-ion population at that location
and is charge-state-summed; it is neither a density of neutral xenon nor an
integral over a flux surface or volume.

This is the xenon-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It is the
on-axis counterpart of [xenon density](name:xenon_density), which applies at
a general plasma location, and it is distinguished from [argon density at
the magnetic axis](name:argon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts a
different ion species.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective kinematic diffusion coefficient for redistribution of the
major-radius component of momentum carried by ions of one specified species
and charge state.
items.documentation:
This coefficient governs diffusive redistribution of the major-radius
component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one specified
species and charge state. The major-radius direction is the direction of
increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local flow-gradient closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_s n_s D_{s,R}\,\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\nabla v_{s,R}
$$

where $s$ identifies the selected ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of its major-radius
momentum through an oriented surface, $m_s$ is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the
charge-state number density, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusion coefficient,
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the surface's unit normal, $\nabla$ is the
spatial-gradient operator, and $v_{s,R}$ is the major-radius component of
the charge-state mean flow velocity.

The radial qualifier selects the transported momentum component, not the
direction of the flux or velocity gradient. It therefore does not prescribe
flux-surface-normal or magnetic-field-perpendicular transport. The
coefficient is charge-state resolved, neither summed nor averaged over
charge states, and excludes convective momentum transport, residual stress,
and external momentum sources.

It is a component-resolved specialization of [effective ion-state momentum
diffusivity](name:effective_ion_state_momentum_diffusivity). The
corresponding [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
applies to the field-parallel momentum component instead.

items.name: mode_reference_phase
items.description:
Mode reference phase is the signed angular offset that sets the complex
phase origin of an oscillatory mode relative to its zero-phase reference. It
shifts the represented mode in phase without changing its amplitude,
frequency, or mode identifiers.
items.documentation:
Mode reference phase is the scalar phase offset applied to the complex
representation of an oscillatory mode to define its phase origin. It is a
representation parameter for the mode as a whole, not a local value of the
oscillating physical field.

A modal perturbation can be represented with the reference phase added to
the modal phase argument:

$$
\delta f(\xi) = \Re\left\{\hat{f}(\xi)\exp\left[i\left(\Theta(\xi,t)+\varphi_\mathrm{ref}\right)\right]\right\}
$$

where $\delta f$ is the physical perturbation, $\hat{f}$ is its complex mode
amplitude, $\Theta$ is the modal phase argument excluding the reference
offset, and $\varphi_\mathrm{ref}$ is the mode reference phase.

This quantity fixes the arbitrary complex phase gage of a mode
representation; it does not define the mode frequency, mode number,
amplitude, or spatial eigenfunction. The [MHD mode reference
phase](name:mhd_mode_reference_phase) is the magnetohydrodynamic
specialization of this generic mode-level quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the offset increases the modal phase argument
in the complex exponential representation.

items.name: force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Force of a poloidal-field coil is the signed electromagnetic load obtained
as a force-combination-matrix linear combination of the coil's radial and
vertical Lorentz-force components in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation:
Force of a poloidal-field coil is a signed scalar electromagnetic load on an
individual poloidal-field coil. It is the Lorentz-force resultant selected
by a force-combination matrix from the coil's radial and vertical force
components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The force-combination definition is

$$
F_{c\ell} = C_{\ell R} F_{R,c} + C_{\ell Z} F_{Z,c}
$$

where $F_{c\ell}$ is this force for coil $c$ and force-combination row
$\ell$, $C_{\ell R}$ and $C_{\ell Z}$ are the radial and vertical
coefficients of the force-combination matrix, $F_{R,c}$ is the [radial force
of a poloidal-field coil](name:radial_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), and
$F_{Z,c}$ is the [vertical force of a poloidal-field
coil](name:vertical_force_of_poloidal_field_coil).

The scope is one poloidal-field coil and one force-combination row; no
summation over multiple coils is implied. This quantity is distinct from the
radial and vertical component forces themselves, and it is not a magnetic
field, current, torque, or structural stress.

The [minimum force of a poloidal-field
coil](name:minimum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil) and [maximum force of a
poloidal-field coil](name:maximum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil) are lower
and upper bounds on this same force-combination scalar.

Sign convention: Positive when $C_{\ell R}F_{R,c}+C_{\ell Z}F_{Z,c}>0$ after
taking $F_{R,c}$ positive outward toward increasing $R$ and $F_{Z,c}$
positive upward toward increasing $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: argon_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Argon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive ionization states
and excluding neutral argon atoms.
items.documentation:
Argon density at a limiter is the local number density of argon ions in the
boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The
evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance, and neutral argon atoms are excluded.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\sum_{q>0} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}(\mathbf{r}_L)
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ are number densities in
m$^{-3}$, $q$ is the positive argon ionization state, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is
the limiter-side position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

This is the argon-specific member of [density at a
limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It counts argon ions rather than the
electrons represented by [electron density at a
limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter), and is local rather than the
flux-surface average represented by flux-surface-averaged argon density at
the plasma boundary.

items.name: perturbed_plasma_temperature_imaginary_part
items.description:
Quadrature (out-of-phase) component of the complex first-order
plasma-temperature eigenfunction for one toroidal Fourier harmonic in linear
MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
The imaginary component of the complex first-order plasma-temperature
eigenfunction for a single toroidal Fourier harmonic in linear MHD. It is
the quadrature component relative to the real component under the selected
Fourier phase convention.

The defining decomposition is:

$$
\delta T = \delta T_R + i\,\delta T_I
$$

where $\delta T$ is the complex temperature amplitude, $\delta T_R$ is its
real component, $\delta T_I$ is the imaginary component represented by this
quantity, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

Together with the [real component of the perturbed plasma
temperature](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part), this quantity
reconstructs the complex perturbed plasma temperature. In the perturbation
$T=T_0+\delta T e^{i(n\phi-\omega t)}$, $T_0$ is the equilibrium
temperature, $n$ is the toroidal mode number, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\omega$ is the complex
eigenfrequency, and $t$ is time. Its value depends on the selected Fourier
phase origin and does not by itself represent the complete physical
temperature perturbation.

items.name: lower_bound_wavelength_of_visible_camera
items.description:
Short-wavelength boundary of the spectral sensitivity band accepted by a
visible-camera detector channel, defining the lower edge of its response
interval. Photons with shorter wavelengths are outside the specified
detector response interval.
items.documentation:
Short-wavelength boundary of the spectral sensitivity band accepted by a
visible-camera detector channel is the minimum photon wavelength included in
the specified detector response interval. It defines an interval endpoint of
the spectral sensitivity band, not the value of the detector response at
that endpoint.

Together with the upper-bound wavelength, it delimits the nominal accepted
wavelength interval. Photons with wavelengths shorter than this lower bound
are outside the specified interval; photons within the interval remain
subject to the detector spectral response function. It is distinct from the
central wavelength and the wavelength bandwidth, which summarize the
interval rather than define its short-wavelength edge.

items.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the
magnetic axis, combining all ionization states.
items.documentation:
The carbon impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis is projected
onto the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame. It represents the density-weighted mean flow of the carbon ion
population rather than a simple average of charge-state velocities.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{C},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{C},q}}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}}$ and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{C},q}$ are toroidal
velocities in m s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{C},q}$ is the number density in
m$^{-3}$, and $q$ indexes carbon ionization states. The quantity includes
all carbon ion charge states and excludes neutral carbon. Its boundary
counterpart is [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary), while the
corresponding magnetic-axis quantity for another impurity is [toroidal
nitrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when $V_{\phi,\mathrm{C}}$ points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_particle_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective advective velocity vector whose product with electron number
density gives the convective electron particle flux, excluding
density-gradient-driven diffusion.
items.documentation:
Electron particle convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient of
the density-proportional advective electron particle flux. It describes
directed electron transport after density-gradient-driven diffusion has been
separated.

The convective electron particle flux is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_e\mathbf{v}_e^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the electron particle flux
due to convection, $n_e$ is the electron number density, and
$\mathbf{v}_e^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this electron particle convection
velocity.

The quantity applies to the electron particle channel without selecting a
directional projection. It is an effective coefficient for the electron
population, not a sum over particle species or an energy- or
momentum-transport coefficient. The [ion particle convection
velocity](name:ion_particle_convection_velocity) is the corresponding
coefficient for the ion particle channel, not a contribution to this
electron coefficient.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and need
not equal the bulk electron flow velocity. The [parallel electron particle
convection velocity](name:parallel_electron_particle_convection_velocity)
and [poloidal electron particle convection
velocity](name:poloidal_electron_particle_convection_velocity) are
projections of this vector along the magnetic field and in the poloidal
direction, respectively, in edge-plasma particle transport.

Sign convention: Positive when the projected electron convective particle
flux points along the positive direction of the corresponding component; the
direction follows electron particle transport, not conventional electric
current.

items.name: length_of_interferometer_beam
items.description:
Length of an interferometer beam is the signed beam-level optical
path-length difference produced by plasma, relative to the corresponding
no-plasma reference for the same interferometer beam. It denotes the
family-level interferometric length signal, not the unperturbed geometric
beam length.
items.documentation:
Length of an interferometer beam is the signed optical path-length
difference assigned to a complete interferometer beam by comparing
propagation through plasma with the corresponding no-plasma reference for
that same beam. It is a beam-level interferometric length quantity, not the
geometric length of the beam trajectory.

For a beam $b$, the quantity is defined as the difference between the plasma
and reference effective optical path lengths:

$$
\Delta L_b = L_{\mathrm{eff},b} - L_{\mathrm{ref},b}
$$

where $\Delta L_b$ is the length of the interferometer beam,
$L_{\mathrm{eff},b}$ is the effective optical path length for beam $b$ with
plasma present, and $L_{\mathrm{ref},b}$ is the corresponding no-plasma
reference effective optical path length for the same beam.

The scope is the complete interferometer beam path, with the plasma
contribution accumulated over that beam as a whole. This quantity excludes
local refractive-index perturbation, phase shift, line-integrated density,
absolute effective optical path length, and unperturbed geometric path
length.

The more specific [length variation of interferometer
beam](name:length_variation_of_interferometer_beam) uses variation
terminology for this same signed difference relative to the reference path;
this entry is the parent family quantity for interferometer-beam optical
path-length changes.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective optical path length with plasma
present is greater than the corresponding no-plasma reference effective
optical path length.

items.name: etendue_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Geometric optical throughput of a soft X-ray detector channel, set by the
collecting area and accepted solid angle of its optical system.
items.documentation:
Etendue is the geometric throughput of the complete optical system serving a
soft X-ray detector channel. It characterizes the channel's acceptance of
radiation by combining its collecting area with the range of accepted
propagation directions.

For the channel optical system, etendue $G$ is defined by

$$
G = A\Omega
$$

where $A$ is the effective collecting area of the detector or aperture and
$\Omega$ is the accepted solid angle subtended by that area.

This quantity applies to the specified soft X-ray detector channel and
represents the geometric optical factor for that channel as a whole. It
excludes the radiation radiance, spectral response, detector conversion
efficiency, and other non-geometrical response factors.

The same geometric throughput concept is used for other diagnostic systems,
including [hard X-ray detector etendue](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector)
and [bolometer etendue](name:etendue_of_bolometer); those quantities differ
by the owning diagnostic object rather than by the defining relation.

items.name: net_efficiency_of_plant_system
items.description:
Dimensionless ratio quantifying how effectively a plant system delivers
signed net electrical power to an external load relative to the total
internal electrical consumption needed to operate it.
items.documentation:
The net efficiency of a plant system is the dimensionless ratio of signed
net electrical power exported outside the plant boundary to total internal
electrical power consumed by plant systems over the same accounting
interval. It is the net-electrical-gain specialization of [efficiency of a
plant system](name:efficiency_of_plant_system), with recirculating
electrical loads included in the net exported power balance.

The defining relation, including the corresponding net-power balance, is:

$$
\eta_{\mathrm{net,plant}} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{net}}}{P_{\mathrm{cons}}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{net}} = P_{\mathrm{gen}} - P_{\mathrm{int}}, \qquad
P_{\mathrm{cons}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}} P_{\mathrm{load},i}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net electrical power of the plant system in
W, $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is the positive total electrical consumption
represented by [power of the plant system](name:power_of_plant_system) in W,
$P_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is gross generated electrical power in W,
$P_{\mathrm{int}}$ is the internal operational electrical consumption
subtracted in the net-power balance in W, $P_{\mathrm{load},i}$ is the
electrical consumption of included load $i$ in W, and
$\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{plant}}$ is the set of electrically powered plant
loads included in the accounting boundary.

The denominator $P_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is a gross positive consumption
quantity, not the signed net exchange $P_{\mathrm{net}}$ and not the gross
generated power $P_{\mathrm{gen}}$. It equals the internal-consumption term
$P_{\mathrm{int}}$ only when the same loads, plant boundary, and interval
define both the net-power balance and the denominator. Unlike [thermal
efficiency of the plant system](name:thermal_efficiency_of_plant_system),
this quantity relates net electrical export to internal electrical
consumption rather than gross electrical output to thermal input.

Sign convention: Positive when signed net electrical power is exported from
the plant system to an external electrical network or load.

items.name: vertical_angle_of_detector_pixel
items.description:
Signed elevation angle of a camera pixel’s line of sight relative to the
camera optical axis, specifying its vertical position within the field of
view.
items.documentation:
The vertical viewing angle of a camera pixel is the signed elevation offset
of its line of sight from the camera optical axis. It specifies angular
position in the camera’s vertical image direction, rather than the full
vertical field-of-view span described by [vertical angular width of
camera](name:vertical_angular_width_of_camera).

In the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ frame, let
$\hat{\ell}$ be the pixel line-of-sight unit vector, $\hat{o}$ the
optical-axis unit vector, and $\hat{v}$ the camera image-up unit vector. The
angle is defined by

$$
\alpha_v = \operatorname{atan2}(\hat{\ell}\cdot\hat{v},\hat{\ell}\cdot\hat{o})
$$

where $\alpha_v$ is the signed vertical viewing angle and the three hatted
quantities are dimensionless unit vectors. The image-up orientation
determines the vertical angular direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the pixel line of sight has a positive
projection onto the camera image-up direction relative to the optical axis.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tungsten_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Dimensionless tungsten abundance ratio equal to the plasma-volume-averaged
elemental tungsten density divided by the plasma-volume-averaged electron
density.
items.documentation:
Dimensionless tungsten abundance ratio equal to the plasma-volume-averaged
elemental tungsten density divided by the plasma-volume-averaged electron
density. It compares the charge-state-summed tungsten-ion population with
the free-electron population in the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined from the two volume averages over the plasma volume $V$
as

$$
a_{\mathrm{W},V}
=
\frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
=
\frac{V^{-1}\int_V \sum_{z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV}{V^{-1}\int_V n_e(\mathbf{x})\, dV}
$$

where $a_{\mathrm{W},V}$ denotes this tungsten abundance ratio, $V$ denotes
the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface over which both
averages are formed, $\langle n_{\mathrm{W}}\rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density),
$\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density),
$n_{\mathrm{W}^{z+}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local number density of tungsten
ions in charge state $z$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the
local free-electron number density, $z=1,\ldots,74$ indexes the positive
tungsten ionization states, and $dV$ is the volume element.

The scope is the confined plasma volume: both numerator and denominator use
the same volume and the same volume-averaging operation. The tungsten
population is elemental tungsten in positive ionization states, summed over
charge state; neutral tungsten is excluded. The aggregation is the ratio of
the two volume averages, not the volume average of the local ratio
$n_{\mathrm{W}}/n_e$, and the quantity is defined only when $\langle
n_e\rangle_V$ is nonzero.

This ratio is an unweighted tungsten-nucleus abundance relative to free
electrons; it is not a charge-weighted tungsten contribution to electron
density and is not an effective-charge measure. It is the tungsten member of
the same volume-averaged composition-ratio family as the [deuterium-tritium
abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
and the [carbon abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_carbon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which replace the tungsten numerator with the corresponding species volume
average while retaining the same electron-density denominator.

items.name: mhd_mode_number
items.description:
Dimensionless mode-number vector labeling the radial branch and poloidal and
toroidal periodicities of a linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the collection of discrete mode labels that identifies a
linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation across its radial, poloidal, and
toroidal structure. It is a mode-index vector, not a spatial wavevector or a
physical displacement vector.

$$
\mathbf{N} = (n_r, m, n_\phi)
$$

where $n_r$ is the non-negative radial branch index, $m$ is the integer
poloidal Fourier harmonic, and $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier
harmonic. The components correspond to the [radial mode
number](name:radial_mode_number), [poloidal mode
number](name:poloidal_mode_number), and [toroidal MHD mode
number](name:toroidal_mhd_mode_number).

The radial index labels branch structure by radial nodes, while the angular
indices label periodicity around the poloidal and toroidal coordinates.
Coupled poloidal harmonics may belong to one eigenmode, so this quantity
identifies the mode labels without requiring a single separable spatial
harmonic.

items.name: volume_averaged_beryllium_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged number density of beryllium impurity ions over the confined
plasma volume, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral
beryllium atoms.
items.documentation:
The volume-averaged beryllium ion number density quantifies the mean
beryllium impurity content throughout the confined plasma volume. It is the
volume average of the local [beryllium ion number
density](name:beryllium_density), rather than a value at a particular
position or along a diagnostic chord.

$$
\overline{n}_\mathrm{Be} = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Be}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}} \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume
element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the local
number density of beryllium ions with charge state $z+$, with $z=1$ through
$4$. Neutral beryllium is excluded. The resulting global quantity is
distinct from the [line-averaged beryllium
density](name:line_averaged_beryllium_density) and provides the numerator
for the [ratio of volume-averaged beryllium density to volume-averaged
electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_beryllium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

items.name: current_density_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive
items.description:
Vector current-density contribution produced by bootstrap and externally
driven non-inductive mechanisms, excluding current generated by an inductive
electric field.
items.documentation:
Non-inductive current density is the vector contribution to plasma electric
current produced without inductive electric-field drive. It includes
bootstrap current and externally driven non-inductive sources, but excludes
the inductive contribution to the total plasma current.

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{NI}} = \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{bootstrap}} + \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{external,NI}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{NI}}$ is the non-inductive current-density
vector, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{bootstrap}}$ is the bootstrap-current density,
and $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{external,NI}}$ is the combined current density from
externally driven non-inductive sources. The [parallel non-inductive current
density](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive)
is a field-aligned, flux-surface-averaged projection of this broader
quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved current-density component points
along the positive direction of its defining axis in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: total_co_passing_particle_density
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged number density of a selected species on untrapped
orbits circulating with the plasma current, including thermal and nonthermal
particles; the corresponding local density is defined at each point before
averaging over its magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Total co-passing particle density is the number density contributed by
particles of a selected species whose untrapped guiding-center orbits
circulate in the direction of the plasma current. It includes thermal and
nonthermal particles and may be specified locally or as a flux-surface
average.

The local density is the velocity-space integral over this orbit class, and
its flux-surface average is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
n_{s,\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) &= \int_{\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \\
\bar n_{s,\mathrm{co}} &= \left\langle n_{s,\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $n_{s,\mathrm{co}}$ is the local co-passing number density, $\bar
n_{s,\mathrm{co}}$ is its flux-surface average, and $s$ labels the selected
species. The distribution function of species $s$ is $f_s$; $\mathbf{x}$ is
position; $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity; $d^3v$ is the velocity-space
volume element; and $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the
velocity-space region associated with untrapped orbits circulating with the
plasma current. The brackets denote a normalized average over the magnetic
flux surface through $\mathbf{x}$, and $\mathrm{FS}$ denotes that surface.

The local form applies at a spatial point, while the averaged form applies
over the magnetic flux surface through that point; the averaged form is not
a local point value. Thermal and nonthermal particles of the selected
species contribute additively, and the quantity is not summed over different
species. It excludes the [total counter-passing particle
density](name:total_counter_passing_particle_density) and [total trapped
particle density](name:total_trapped_particle_density), which describe
distinct orbit classes.

At matching local or flux-surface-averaged scope, [co-passing fast-particle
density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density) is the suprathermal
contribution included here. This co-passing orbit-class contribution is part
of [particle density](name:particle_density), which also includes other
particle populations.

items.name: parallel_plasma_velocity
items.description:
Parallel component of the bulk plasma center-of-mass velocity along the
local magnetic-field direction, representing field-aligned mass transport of
all contributing species.
items.documentation:
The parallel plasma velocity is the projection of the bulk [plasma
velocity](name:plasma_velocity) onto the local magnetic-field direction. It
represents the mass-weighted flow of all contributing plasma species along
magnetic field lines.

The parallel component is defined by:

$$
v_\parallel = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{cm} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{cm}$ is the center-of-mass plasma velocity,
$\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its
magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the corresponding unit vector. Unlike
the [radial plasma velocity](name:radial_plasma_velocity), this quantity
follows the local magnetic-field direction rather than the outward
major-radius direction.

The quantity is a bulk-plasma projection, not a species-resolved flow or a
diamagnetic-drift velocity.

items.name: ion_power_density
items.description:
Net rate of energy transfer to or from an ion population per unit physical
volume, summed over its ionic charge states and the included energy-transfer
processes.
items.documentation:
Ion power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from
an ion population per unit physical volume. It is the source or sink term
for that recipient population in its energy balance.

The volumetric power density is defined by

$$
Q_i = \frac{dP_i}{dV}
$$

where $Q_i$ is the ion power density, $P_i$ is the net power transferred to
