the selected ion population within physical volume $V$, and the subscript
$i$ identifies the ion recipient.

The recipient may be a specified ion species or an aggregate of species,
with contributions summed over all ionic charge states of each included
species. The net source combines the included energy-transfer processes; it
does not inherently require every heating or loss mechanism. Unlike [ion
charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), it does
not resolve individual charge states or charge-state bundles.

This quantity is neither stored ion energy nor volume-integrated power. It
is also distinct from the complete rate of change of ion energy, which
includes transport contributions. Energy transferred to electron or neutral
recipients is excluded.

[Fast-ion power density](name:fast_ion_power_density) specializes this
quantity to coherent-wave energy deposition into nonthermal ions of a
specified species. [Total ion power density](name:total_ion_power_density)
instead aggregates the net energy-transfer rate over all included ion
species and charge states.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is transferred to the selected ion
population; negative when energy is removed from it.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_line_of_sight
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the second reference point on a line of sight,
equal to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of line of sight

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal coordinates of the second reference
point in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, with $z$ the vertical
coordinate and the $z$ axis coinciding with the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is nonnegative and vanishes on the toroidal symmetry axis. It
is distinct from a distance along the line of sight, a minor-radius distance
measured from the magnetic axis, and a magnetic flux label. Like the [radial
coordinate of a measurement
position](name:radial_coordinate_of_measurement_position), it locates a
specified point; no summation, line integration, averaging, or emission
weighting is implied.

items.name: current_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Net conventional electric current delivered by the plasma to one divertor
target surface is integrated over the wetted strike zone. Ion and electron
contributions are combined with their electric-charge signs, so this is not
an unsigned particle flux.
items.documentation:
Net conventional electric current delivered by the plasma to one divertor
target surface is the signed charge-flow rate crossing the plasma-facing
target interface, integrated over the wetted strike zone. It represents the
net incident conventional current carried by charged plasma particles to
that target.

The target current is defined by the surface integral of incident
conventional-current density over the wetted target region:

$$
I_{\mathrm{target}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{wet}}} \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{target}} \, dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the current at the divertor target,
$S_{\mathrm{wet}}$ is the wetted strike-zone part of the target surface,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident conventional electric-current
density due to plasma particles at the target surface,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the unit normal directed from the
plasma into the target material, and $dA$ is the surface area element. For
multiple charged species, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the charge-weighted
sum of their incident particle flux densities, so ion and electron
contributions enter with opposite electric-charge signs.

The scope is one physical divertor target surface; the aggregation
convention is the surface integral over the wetted strike-zone region of
that target. It excludes neighboring targets, non-target plasma-facing
components, and return currents in external conducting structures. It is a
net conventional current, not an ion-only current, an electron-only current,
an unsigned collected-current magnitude, or a particle flux.

Summing this quantity over the target surfaces belonging to a divertor gives
the target-current contribution to [current of
divertor](name:current_of_divertor). If a target is partitioned into tiles,
summing [current of divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile) over the
tiles that cover the same wetted target region gives this per-target
quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional current carried by
charged plasma particles is directed from the plasma into the divertor
target material.

items.name: volume_averaged_xenon_density
items.description:
Number density of xenon ions averaged over the full plasma volume, including
all charged xenon ionization states and excluding neutral xenon.
items.documentation:
The volume-averaged xenon ion number density is the plasma-wide mean of the
local [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which sums xenon ions from singly
ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral atoms.

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the volume-averaged xenon ion density,
$n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local xenon ion density at position
$\mathbf{r}$, $V_p$ is the full plasma volume, and $dV$ is the physical
volume element. The averaging is over the plasma volume rather than along a
measurement chord or at a single locus. The resulting global
impurity-content measure can be compared with electron content through the
ratio of volume-averaged xenon density to volume-averaged electron density.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_of_flux_loop
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux of an individual flux loop is the measured, signed
vertical-field integral over a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal
symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux of an individual flux loop is the signed poloidal
flux represented by that loop's measured value.

For an axisymmetric magnetic field, its defining relation is

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p}} = 2\pi \int_0^{R_\ell} B_Z(R', Z_\ell)\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux, $B_Z$ is the
vertical magnetic-field component, and $R'$ is the integration radius. In
the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $R_\ell$ and $Z_\ell$ specify
the evaluation location at the flux loop. The integration disk has its
positive normal toward increasing $Z$.

This is the loop-specific value of [poloidal magnetic
flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), not a sum or average over multiple
loops. It represents an integrated flux rather than a local magnetic-field
value and is distinct from [toroidal magnetic
flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when the net magnetic flux through the integration
disk is directed toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: xenon_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Xenon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over
all xenon ionization states.
items.documentation:
Xenon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local
concentration of xenon ions with all positive charge states combined.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the total xenon ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is the number density of xenon ions with charge state
$z$, and $z$ is the positive integer xenon charge state.

The quantity applies locally at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, the
inner shoulder of the edge transport barrier, whose position is defined by
the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over xenon ions from the singly ionized through fully ionized states
and excludes neutral xenon; it is not a chord, flux-surface, or volume
average.

This is the xenon-specific component of the total [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), whereas [xenon
density](name:xenon_density) denotes the corresponding local xenon ion
density without fixing the pedestal-top locus. The same charge-state
aggregation evaluated at another boundary location is given by [xenon
density at the plasma boundary](name:xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Toroidal angular coordinate of each antenna-strap outline point around the
machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal angle is the azimuthal coordinate assigned to each point on the
geometric outline of an antenna strap. It identifies the point’s
circumferential location in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to individual strap-outline points and is not a mean,
sum, nominal center coordinate, or mechanical orientation angle. No
aggregation over the outline is implied; each point retains its own $\phi$
value.

Together with the other coordinates of the outline, this angle locates the
strap geometry. It is distinct from the [radial coordinate of the antenna
strap](name:radial_coordinate_of_antenna_strap), which locates a strap
reference point, while [vertical outline of the antenna
strap](name:vertical_outline_of_antenna_strap) provides the corresponding
signed vertical coordinate for outline points. The same angular-coordinate
concept is used for a different object by [toroidal angle of a coil
conductor element](name:toroidal_angle_of_coil_conductor_element).

Sign convention: Positive when the angular displacement from the chosen
$\phi=0$ reference is toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+Z$.

items.name: plasma_pressure_imaginary_part
items.description:
Plasma pressure imaginary part is the scalar coefficient multiplying the
imaginary unit in a complex representation of isotropic plasma pressure. It
is a phase-quadrature part of the pressure representation, not the complete
complex pressure quantity.
items.documentation:
Plasma pressure imaginary part is the scalar coefficient multiplying the
imaginary unit in a complex representation of isotropic plasma pressure. It
represents the imaginary phase quadrature of that pressure representation
and is not the complete complex pressure quantity.

A complex plasma-pressure quantity is decomposed into real and imaginary
quadratures as:

$$
p = p_\mathrm{R} + i\,p_\mathrm{I}
$$

where $p$ is the complex plasma-pressure quantity, $i$ is the imaginary
unit, $p_\mathrm{R}$ is its real-part quadrature, and $p_\mathrm{I}$ is the
plasma pressure imaginary part defined here.

This parent quantity applies to any complex scalar representation of
isotropic plasma pressure. It does not by itself specify perturbation order,
Fourier mode number, reference phase, eigenfunction normalization, or
spatial dependence.

The perturbation-specific [perturbed plasma pressure imaginary
part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_imaginary_part) is a specialization of
this parent in which $p$ is restricted to the complex first-order
plasma-pressure perturbation eigenfunction. The quantity is distinct from
plasma pressure, which denotes the pressure scalar itself rather than the
imaginary quadrature of a complex representation.

Sign convention: Positive when the pressure phasor projects onto the $+i$
direction of the complex plane.

items.name: ion_absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Total coherent electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly to ion
populations, integrated over the plasma volume and partitioned into thermal
and fast-ion contributions.
items.documentation:
Ion absorbed wave power is the total rate of energy transfer from coherent
electromagnetic waves to ion populations. It includes direct absorption by
both bulk thermal ions and suprathermal fast ions.

The volume-integrated ion power is defined by

$$
P_i^{\mathrm{abs}} = \int_V p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{abs}} + P_{i,\mathrm{thermal}}^{\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_i^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total ion absorbed wave power,
$p_i^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local wave power deposition density
to ions, $V$ is the plasma volume, and the two terms are the [fast-ion
absorbed wave power](name:fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [thermal-ion
absorbed wave power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power). This quantity is
the ion component of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power),
excluding power transferred directly to electron populations; [electron
absorbed wave power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power) represents the
corresponding electron channel.

items.name: spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Energy-resolved probability that a photon incident on a soft X-ray detector
produces a registered event, defining the detector’s spectral response.
items.documentation:
The spectral detection efficiency is the probability that an incident photon
at a specified energy produces a registered detector event. It characterizes
the detector response, rather than the incident photon flux or the emitted
X-ray radiance.

The efficiency is defined by

$$
\eta(E) = \frac{N_{\mathrm{registered}}(E)}{N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)}
$$

where $E$ is photon energy, $N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)$ is the number of
photons incident at that energy, and $N_{\mathrm{registered}}(E)$ is the
number producing registered events. For a probability-based detector
response, $0 \leq \eta(E) \leq 1$. The energy dependence distinguishes this
quantity from the band-integrated [power of the soft X-ray
detector](name:power_of_soft_xray_detector) and makes it the soft-X-ray
counterpart of [spectral efficiency of the hard X-ray
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector).

items.name: poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming bound on poloidal ion
momentum flux in edge-plasma transport, limiting its magnitude without
reversing its direction.
items.documentation:
The poloidal ion momentum flux-limiter coefficient sets the collisionless
free-streaming bound on the poloidal component of gradient-driven ion
[momentum](name:momentum) transport in edge-plasma fluid closures. The
poloidal direction follows a magnetic-flux-surface contour in a plane
containing the toroidal symmetry axis, rather than the toroidal or
flux-surface-normal direction.

The coefficient defines the upper bound:

$$
\left|\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}\right| \leq \alpha_{i,\mathrm{p}}\,\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited poloidal ion
momentum flux, $\alpha_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is this nonnegative limiter
coefficient, and $\Pi_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative
collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude specified by the momentum
closure. The subscripts $i$ and $\mathrm{p}$ identify ions and the poloidal
component. Limiting preserves the direction of the original flux; the bound
does not prescribe a particular interpolation formula.

This coefficient applies at the ion-species level rather than to an
individually resolved charge state. It is a closure parameter, not a sum of
charge-state coefficients, and it excludes electron and neutral momentum
transport. It controls a flux bound rather than the momentum diffusivity
that determines the unrestricted gradient-driven flux.

It is the poloidal member of the component-resolved [ion momentum
flux-limiter coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). The
[poloidal neutral momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) serves
the corresponding limiting role for neutral momentum transport, not for
ions.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Vertical position of the geometric center of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe, expressed as its signed Z coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical position of the geometric center of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe is the signed height coordinate of the probe center in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It locates the probe center
along the vertical direction and does not define the orientation of the
probe's sensitive axis or the magnetic-field component measured by the
probe.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major
radius from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$
the vertical coordinate, the probe-center coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{probe}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{probe}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is the vertical coordinate of the poloidal
magnetic-field probe center, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{probe}}$ is the position
vector of that geometric center relative to the coordinate origin, and
$\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector.

This quantity applies to the geometric center of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe as a physical object. For a probe with finite extent, it refers to the
center position rather than to the probe size, winding distribution, support
structure, or any spatial average of the measured magnetic field.

Together with the [radial coordinate of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), it
specifies the probe-center position in the $(R,Z)$ poloidal cross-section at
a given toroidal angle. The same signed-coordinate concept is used for other
magnetic diagnostic objects, such as the [vertical coordinate of a toroidal
magnetic-field
probe](name:vertical_coordinate_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), the
[vertical coordinate of a flux loop](name:vertical_coordinate_of_flux_loop),
and the [vertical coordinate of a Rogowski
coil](name:vertical_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil), but those names apply to
different objects.

Sign convention: Positive when the probe-center position lies above the
machine midplane in the $+Z$ direction.

items.name: radiative_extraordinary_mode_temperature_at_ece_channel
items.description:
Predicted equivalent blackbody temperature of extraordinary-mode electron
cyclotron emission evaluated at a frequency-selective ECE channel.
items.documentation:
The extraordinary-mode radiative temperature is the blackbody-equivalent
temperature assigned to the predicted electron cyclotron emission in the
extraordinary polarization at an ECE channel. It represents radiation
intensity, not the kinetic temperature of the emitting electrons.

The defining radiance equivalence is

$$
I_{\nu,X} = B_\nu\left(T_{\mathrm{rad},X}\right)
$$

where $I_{\nu,X}$ is the predicted extraordinary-mode spectral radiance,
$\nu$ is the channel's selected emission frequency, $X$ identifies the
extraordinary polarization, $B_\nu$ is the blackbody spectral-radiance
function, and $T_{\mathrm{rad},X}$ is the corresponding radiative
temperature.

This quantity is resolved for the extraordinary polarization and evaluated
at the frequency associated with one ECE channel; it is not a sum over
channels, polarizations, or emission modes, and it excludes the
ordinary-mode contribution. The [radiative ordinary-mode temperature at an
ECE channel](name:radiative_ordinary_mode_temperature_at_ece_channel) is the
corresponding ordinary-polarization quantity, while [radiative temperature
at an ECE channel](name:radiative_temperature_at_ece_channel) denotes the
channel-level radiation temperature without this extraordinary-mode
restriction. Differences between the predicted extraordinary-mode value and
a measured channel radiation temperature can indicate mode coupling or
optical-depth effects.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_camera
items.description:
Major-radius location of a camera’s geometric center, measured from the
toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial coordinate of a camera is the major-radius position of its
geometric center, measured perpendicular to the toroidal symmetry axis. It
identifies the camera center rather than any individual detector pixel,
aperture, or line-of-sight point.

The coordinate is defined from the Cartesian coordinates of the camera
center:

$$
R_{\mathrm{cam}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{cam}}^2 + y_{\mathrm{cam}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{cam}}$ is the camera-center radial coordinate, and
$x_{\mathrm{cam}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{cam}}$ are the camera-center coordinates
in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis. The
corresponding cylindrical frame is the right-handed $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

This quantity applies to the geometric center of the camera as a whole and
is not an average over pixels, viewing directions, or detector elements. It
is the camera-specific specialization of the parent [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate). Together with the [vertical coordinate
of the camera](name:vertical_coordinate_of_camera) and [toroidal coordinate
of the camera](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_camera), it specifies the
camera-center position.

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_aperture
items.description:
Signed coordinate of each aperture-outline vertex along the aperture’s
second local tangential axis, defining its location in the object-local
cross-sectional geometry.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed position of an aperture-outline vertex projected
onto the second local tangential axis of the aperture’s object-local $(X_1,
X_2)$ frame. Together with the first local tangential coordinate, it defines
the boundary geometry of the aperture.

The coordinate of vertex $v$ is defined by

$$
x_{2,v} = (\mathbf{r}_v - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{X}}_2
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the position of the outline vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$
is the origin of the local frame, and $\hat{\mathbf{X}}_2$ is its second
local tangential unit vector. This object-local axis is distinct from
machine radial, toroidal, and vertical directions. The same ordinal-axis
convention applies to the [second local tangential coordinate of diagnostic
aperture](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture).

items.name: ion_heat_convection_velocity
items.description:
Ion heat convection velocity is the effective vector velocity whose product
with ion thermal-energy density gives the convective flux of ion thermal
energy. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted
mean over all ion charge states and is not assumed to equal the bulk ion
flow velocity.
items.documentation:
Ion heat convection velocity is the effective vector velocity that advects
aggregate ion thermal energy in an ion energy balance. It is a species-level
intensive velocity for the ion population, defined as the density-weighted
mean over all ion charge states.

The defining relation is the convective part of the ion thermal-energy flux:

$$
\mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{E}_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,\mathbf{v}_{Q_i}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of ion thermal
energy, $\mathcal{E}_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the ion thermal-energy density, and
$\mathbf{v}_{Q_i}$ is the ion heat convection velocity.

This quantity is not, by definition, the bulk ion flow velocity or an ion
particle convection velocity; it is defined by the ion thermal-energy flux
decomposition. Component-resolved specializations, such as [parallel ion
heat convection velocity](name:parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity), are
projections of this ion-heat transport velocity and do not change the
charge-state aggregation convention.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{v}_{Q_i}$
points along the positive basis vector for that component, such as
$+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_flux
items.description:
Vertical neutral momentum flux is the signed Z component of the aggregate
momentum-flux vector carried by neutral particles in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It aggregates neutral species and internal
states rather than retaining an individual state contribution.
items.documentation:
Vertical neutral momentum flux is the signed vertical component of the
momentum-flux vector carried by neutral particles. The vertical direction is
parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

The vertical component is the projection of the aggregate neutral
momentum-flux vector:

$$
\Gamma_{0,Z} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,Z}$ is this vertical component, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is
the aggregate [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) vector,
and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the toroidal symmetry
axis. In the stated frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

At a spatial location, this quantity aggregates contributions from neutral
species and internal states; it does not retain an individual state
contribution, unlike [vertical neutral state momentum
flux](name:vertical_neutral_state_momentum_flux). It describes transported
neutral momentum, not a local momentum source or neutral particle flux.

This is the vertical directional component of [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux). In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, [radial neutral momentum
flux](name:radial_neutral_momentum_flux) and [toroidal neutral momentum
flux](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux) are the corresponding components
along the radial and toroidal directions. [Parallel neutral momentum
flux](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_flux) is instead a projection along the
local magnetic-field direction, not a cylindrical component.

Sign convention: Positive when the aggregate neutral momentum-flux vector
has a component toward increasing $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity
items.description:
Poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the poloidal Fickian
diffusivity for thermal-energy transport of a specified ion charge state in
flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ), defined so the diffusive energy flux along
increasing poloidal angle θ at fixed radial flux label ρ and toroidal angle
φ is proportional to and opposite the corresponding gradient of that state's
thermal-energy density.
items.documentation:
Poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusivity is the effective transport
coefficient for local diffusive smoothing of the thermal-energy density of
one specified ion charge state along the poloidal direction in flux
coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It represents the Fickian part of that
charge state's thermal-energy transport along the poloidal coordinate
direction, distinct from convective transport and explicit energy sources,
and is the poloidal component of ion charge-state energy diffusivity.

The defining closure for the poloidal component is

$$
\mathbf{q}_{E,z}\cdot\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}} = -\chi_{E,z}^{\mathrm{pol}}\,\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}\cdot\nabla w_z
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,z}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux density of ion
charge state $z$, $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local unit tangent
generated by increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed radial flux label
$\rho$ and fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta,
\phi)$, $\chi_{E,z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal ion charge-state energy
diffusivity, $w_z$ is the thermal-energy density of that charge state, and
$\hat{e}_{\mathrm{pol}}\cdot\nabla w_z$ is the corresponding poloidal
gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed
over ion species or charge states, unlike [poloidal ion energy
diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity). The field-aligned
directional counterpart is [parallel ion charge-state energy
diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusivity). A
temperature-gradient form is equivalent only when the relevant density and
heat-capacity factors are explicitly included in the coefficient.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged kinetic stress of suprathermal particles of one
species per degree of freedom perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The perpendicular fast-particle pressure is the flux-surface average of the
field-perpendicular component of the gyrotropic kinetic stress carried by
suprathermal particles of a specified species. It represents stress per
transverse degree of freedom, rather than the sum of the two transverse
stresses.

The perpendicular component is defined by the transverse second moment of
the fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{2}\int v_\perp^2 f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular fast-particle
pressure, $s$ labels the specified particle species, $m_s$ is its particle
mass, $f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is its suprathermal distribution function,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v_\perp$ is
the magnitude of the velocity perpendicular to the local magnetic field, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The brackets denote a
normalized flux-surface average with weight proportional to the reciprocal
magnitude of the gradient of a smooth flux-surface label.

This quantity includes only the nonthermal population of the selected
species. Multiple fast-particle populations of that same species are
superposed in the distribution function and therefore contribute additively
to the pressure. It is not a sum over distinct species, is not restricted to
a single orbit class, and excludes the thermal-population pressure. Unlike
the local perpendicular stress, it includes flux-surface averaging.

The corresponding [parallel fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure), denoted by
$p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}$, is the independent field-aligned stress
component. Together they determine the isotropic [fast-particle
pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure), $p_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$, through
$p_s^{\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast}})/3$,
with all three quantities referring to the same species, suprathermal
population, and flux-surface average. The parallel and perpendicular
components need not be equal.

items.name: effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description:
Effective advective drift velocity of neutral particles in a specified
internal state for convective momentum transport; it multiplies the
population's momentum density to form the convective momentum flux.
items.documentation:
Effective advective drift velocity of neutral particles in a specified
internal state for convective momentum transport is the vector transport
coefficient that multiplies the population's momentum-density vector to give
the convective momentum-flux tensor. It represents the advective velocity
appearing in a momentum-transport closure for that resolved neutral
internal-state population.

The convective momentum flux is defined by the outer-product relation

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\alpha} = \boldsymbol{g}_{\alpha} \otimes \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{conv}}_{\alpha}$ is the convective
momentum-flux tensor of neutral particles in internal state $\alpha$,
$\boldsymbol{g}_{\alpha}$ is their momentum-density vector, and
$\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}$ is this effective convective
momentum velocity.

The effective qualifier means the coefficient is defined by this
momentum-flux closure and need not equal the neutral population's
microscopic mean particle velocity. It is the momentum-transport analog of
[effective neutral internal-state velocity due to
convection](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_convection),
which enters the convective particle-flux relation, and is distinguished
from the non-effective counterpart [neutral internal-state momentum velocity
due to
convection](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection).
This name denotes the full vector; [radial effective neutral internal-state
momentum velocity due to
convection](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
denotes its cylindrical $\hat{R}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive when a vector component of
$\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathrm{eff,mom}}_{\alpha}$ is aligned with the positive
direction of the corresponding explicitly chosen basis vector.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Kinematic diffusion coefficient governing down-gradient transport along the
magnetic field of flow momentum carried by ions of one species in a
specified charge state.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the kinematic diffusion
coefficient for down-gradient transport of flow momentum carried by ions of
one species in a specified charge state. Parallel identifies the transport
direction along the local magnetic field, not necessarily the direction of
the transported momentum component.

For a local Fickian description, the parallel diffusive flux of the
represented momentum density is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,\parallel} = -D_{s,\parallel}\nabla_{\parallel} M_s
$$

Here, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,\parallel}$ is the diffusive flux of that
momentum density along the magnetic field, $D_{s,\parallel}$ is this
coefficient, and $M_s$ is the flow-momentum density carried by ion species
and charge state $s$. The index $s$ identifies that species and charge
state. The parallel gradient is $\nabla_{\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf
b}\cdot\nabla$, where $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator. The minus sign
means the diffusive flux is directed down the field-parallel gradient.

The coefficient is resolved for one ion species and one specified charge
state; it is not summed or averaged over species or charge states. It
describes diffusive transport only, not convective transport or total
momentum flux. It is the parallel directional component of the
charge-state-resolved [ion charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), and is distinct
from the [radial ion charge-state momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient),
whose transport direction is cylindrical $\hat R$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(\hat R,\hat\phi,\hat Z)$ basis. Here, $\hat R$, $\hat\phi$,
and $\hat Z$ are the basis directions; $R$ is major radius from the machine
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when
viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective convection coefficient relating the nondiffusive flux of
magnetic-field-parallel momentum to the parallel momentum density of a
specified ion species and charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient governing advective, nondiffusive
transport of magnetic-field-parallel [momentum](name:momentum) carried by
ions of one specified species and charge state. It is a transport-closure
coefficient, not the charge state's bulk parallel flow velocity.

The convective contribution to the parallel-momentum flux is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} g_{s,\parallel}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its convective flux of parallel
momentum in the specified transport direction,
$V_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection coefficient,
and $g_{s,\parallel}$ is its parallel momentum density. The momentum density
is $g_{s,\parallel}=m_s n_s u_{s,\parallel}$, where $m_s$ is the ion mass,
$n_s$ is the number density of that charge state, and $u_{s,\parallel}$ is
its mean flow velocity projected along the local magnetic field.

The parallel label identifies the transported momentum component; it does
not require the transport direction itself to follow the magnetic field. The
coefficient is charge-state resolved, with no sum or average over charge
states implied. It excludes the diffusive and residual-stress contributions
to momentum flux and is distinct from a particle convection coefficient.

This is the parallel-momentum specialization of [ion charge-state momentum
convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity).
Unlike [diamagnetic momentum convection
velocity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity), it does not
specifically isolate a diamagnetic contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the convective parallel-momentum flux in the
specified positive transport direction has the same sign as the parallel
momentum density; the parallel momentum component is positive along the
local magnetic field.

items.name: parallel_neutral_species_particle_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective particle diffusivity for an ion species along the magnetic field,
relating its diffusive particle flux to its parallel number-density
gradient.
items.documentation:
Effective parallel particle diffusivity for an ion species is the
directional transport coefficient that represents ion-particle spreading
driven by that species' number-density gradient. It is the field-parallel
specialization of [ion particle diffusivity](name:ion_particle_diffusivity),
with transport resolved along the magnetic field.

For the field-parallel direction, the diffusive ion-particle flux is defined
by

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\parallel,i}\frac{\partial n_i}{\partial s_{\parallel}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the selected ion species,
$\Gamma_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is its parallel diffusive particle
flux, $D_{\parallel,i}$ is its parallel particle diffusivity, $n_i$ is its
ion number density, and $s_{\parallel}$ is physical arclength along the
magnetic-field direction. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport
for positive diffusivity.

The density and diffusive flux are summed over all ionic charge states of
the selected species, excluding neutral particles. This ion-species scope
differs from [neutral-species particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_species_particle_diffusivity) and its
field-parallel counterpart, [parallel neutral particle
diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity). The coefficient
describes particle diffusion only; it excludes convective particle flux and
is distinct from energy and momentum diffusion coefficients.

items.name: toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of xenon ions at the magnetic axis,
averaged over all xenon ionization states and signed by the toroidal
direction.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the toroidal component of the xenon-ion bulk-flow velocity
evaluated at the magnetic axis. It is the density-weighted mean over all
xenon ionization states; neutral xenon is excluded. The component is defined
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

At the magnetic axis, the charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included xenon ionization states,
$n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density,
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and
$V_{\phi,\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the resulting mean. This quantity differs from
[toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), which is not restricted
to xenon, and from [toroidal xenon velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), which
is evaluated at another locus.

Sign convention: Positive when the xenon-ion flow component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fickian diffusivity governing aggregate neutral-particle transport along the
cylindrical radial direction, relating radial flux to the neutral
number-density gradient.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral diffusion coefficient is the Fickian diffusivity for the
aggregate neutral population, with neutral internal states combined into one
particle population. It is the radial component of the directional quantity
defined by
[neutral_diffusion_coefficient](name:neutral_diffusion_coefficient).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the radial neutral
particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,R} = -D_{n,R}\frac{\partial n_n}{\partial R}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,R}$ is the neutral particle flux in the cylindrical
$\hat{R}$ direction, $D_{n,R}$ is the radial neutral diffusion coefficient,
$n_n$ is the aggregate neutral number density, and $R$ is the major-radius
coordinate. The coefficient applies to particle transport, not to the
separate diffusion of neutral momentum or thermal energy. For passive
Fickian diffusion, $D_{n,R}$ is non-negative.

items.name: parallel_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Field-aligned velocity attributed to an effective diamagnetic
pressure-gradient contribution for one internal state of a neutral species
in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
projection of an effective pressure-gradient transport velocity onto the
local magnetic-field direction. For an uncharged neutral state, it
represents an assigned fluid-transport contribution, not a direct magnetic
guiding-center drift.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},a,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}_{\mathrm{dia},a} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{dia},a,\parallel}$ is the parallel velocity contribution
for the neutral species and internal state labeled $a$,
$\mathbf{v}^{\mathrm{eff}}_{\mathrm{dia},a}$ is its effective diamagnetic
velocity vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local magnetic-field unit
vector. The direction is defined by
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its nonzero magnitude.

This quantity applies locally in the edge plasma to one specified neutral
species and internal quantum state, without summing or averaging over other
states or species. It fixes the field-aligned projection direction left
unspecified by [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

It excludes independent contributions to the total neutral flow and cannot
be obtained by substituting zero charge into the charged-particle
diamagnetic-drift formula. If the assigned effective velocity is strictly
perpendicular to the magnetic field, its parallel projection vanishes; a
transverse projection is instead represented by [perpendicular neutral-state
velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:perpendicular_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

Sign convention: Positive when the effective diamagnetic velocity
contribution has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: derivative_of_poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate
items.description:
Local geometric rate of change of a flux surface’s enclosed poloidal
cross-sectional area as its toroidal-flux coordinate varies.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local geometric rate at which the poloidal
cross-sectional area enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface changes
along the family of surfaces labeled by the toroidal-flux coordinate.

The derivative is defined by:

$$
\frac{dA}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}
$$

where $A$ is the [poloidal-plane cross-sectional area of a flux
surface](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface), and
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal-flux coordinate labeling the nested
surfaces.

The area is enclosed by one closed magnetic-flux-surface contour in a
fixed-toroidal-angle poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height. The quantity applies to one flux surface at a time;
it is not the area of the full three-dimensional flux surface, a derivative
of enclosed volume, or an average over multiple surfaces.

This is the derivative transformation of the cross-sectional-area quantity
linked above. It differs from [the radial derivative of poloidal magnetic
flux](name:radial_derivative_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux), which
differentiates signed poloidal magnetic flux rather than geometric
cross-sectional area.

items.name: toroidal_total_plasma_momentum
items.description:
Total linear momentum of all plasma species projected onto the toroidal
direction by integrating their momentum density over the confined plasma
volume.
items.documentation:
The total toroidal plasma momentum is the integrated linear momentum of all
ion species and electrons projected onto the geometric toroidal direction.
It is the toroidal component of the [total plasma
momentum](name:total_plasma_momentum), not an angular momentum or a local
momentum-flux quantity.

$$
P_\phi = \int_{V_p} \left(\sum_s \boldsymbol{\pi}_s\right) \cdot \hat{\phi}\,dV
$$

where $P_\phi$ is the total toroidal momentum, $V_p$ is the confined plasma
volume, $\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ is the local linear-momentum density of species
$s$, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $dV$ is the volume
element. The toroidal direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

Sign convention: Positive when the integrated linear momentum points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Toroidal fast-particle torque due to collisions is the volume-integrated
toroidal torque exerted on the fast, non-thermal particle population by
Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma. The aggregate
includes thermal electrons and all thermal ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
Toroidal fast-particle torque due to collisions is the volume-integrated
toroidal torque exerted on the fast, non-thermal particle population by
Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma. It is the component
of collisional angular-momentum transfer about the symmetry axis associated
with increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The aggregate torque is defined as the plasma-volume integral of the
toroidal collisional force density weighted by the major radius:

$$
T_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V R \sum_{j \in \mathcal{B}} f_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}\leftarrow j}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $T_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the toroidal fast-particle
torque due to collisions, $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a differential
volume element, $\mathcal{B}$ is the set of thermal-background collision
partners, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{fast}\leftarrow j}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the
toroidal component of the collisional force density exerted on fast,
non-thermal particles by partner $j$.

The set $\mathcal{B}$ contains thermal electrons and every thermal ion
species and every charge state of each thermal ion species; the ion part is
charge-state-summed. This quantity is the aggregate over those collision
partners, not an electron-only or charge-state-resolved contribution; the
thermal-electron collision contribution and the [thermal-ion charge-state
collision
contribution](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions)
sum to it when defined over the same volume and fast-particle population.
The equal-and-opposite collisional angular-momentum transfer to the thermal
background is represented by the
[thermal-electron](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions)
and [thermal-ion](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_due_to_collisions)
reaction channels.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions exert a net toroidal force
on fast, non-thermal particles in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient for the upper outboard quadrant of each
nested flux surface, measuring the departure of that corner from a reference
ellipse with the same center, horizontal half-width, and elongation.
items.documentation:
The upper outer squareness $\zeta_{uo}$ is the dimensionless Luce (2013)
shape coefficient for the upper outboard ($+Z$, large-$R$) corner of each
nested magnetic flux surface, measuring how much that quadrant departs from
a reference ellipse sharing the same geometric center, horizontal
half-width, and elongation. It is one of four quadrant-resolved squareness
parameters — alongside the [lower outer
squareness](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface), [upper inner
squareness](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface), and [lower inner
squareness](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface) — extending the
standard elongation-triangularity shape description to higher order.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the flux-surface
boundary in the upper outer quadrant is described by the Luce
parameterization as:

$$
R = R_\mathrm{geo} + a\cos\!\bigl(\theta + \delta_{uo}\sin\theta + \zeta_{uo}\sin 2\theta\bigr)
$$

with $Z = Z_\mathrm{geo} + \kappa\, a\sin\theta$, where $R_\mathrm{geo}$ and
$Z_\mathrm{geo}$ are the coordinates of the flux-surface geometric center,
$a$ is the minor radius, $\kappa$ is the elongation, $\delta_{uo}$ is the
upper outer triangularity, and $\theta \in [0, \pi/2]$ is the geometric
poloidal angle spanning the upper outboard quadrant.

Values near zero indicate an approximately elliptic corner; positive values
are characteristic of D-shaped cross-sections with a squared-off outboard
corner, while negative values correspond to a more concave or helmet-shaped
upper outer region. The coefficient is extracted from equilibrium
reconstruction by fitting computed flux-surface contours to the Luce
parameterization in the upper outboard region. The symmetric combination of
upper and lower outer quadrant values constitutes the aggregate
[outer_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:outer_squareness_of_flux_surface),
and the value at the outermost flux surface corresponds to
[upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the upper outer corner of the flux surface
protrudes beyond the reference ellipse, giving the cross-section a more
rectangular (D-shaped) outboard corner.

items.name: alpha_angle_of_iron_core_segment
items.description:
Signed inclination of the alpha-side edge of an iron core segment
cross-section, measured from the outward major-radius direction toward
increasing vertical height.
items.documentation:
The alpha angle is the signed orientation of the designated alpha-side edge
of an iron core segment in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It identifies the alpha-side orientation
and is independent of the edge length.

For an oriented alpha-side vector with signed radial and vertical components
$\Delta R$ and $\Delta Z$, the angle is defined by

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}(\Delta Z,\Delta R)
$$

where $\alpha$ is the alpha angle, $\Delta R$ is the component along the
outward major-radius direction, and $\Delta Z$ is the component along the
vertical direction. This quantity is the alpha-side specialization of the
general iron core segment orientation angle, not a length or cross-sectional
dimension.

Sign convention: Positive when the oriented alpha-side vector is inclined
from the outward $+R$ direction toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
items.description:
Radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the R component of the complex
linear-MHD plasma-response perturbation in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the major-radius-directed
component of the complex linear-MHD magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction, or of its corresponding real perturbation, carried by the
confined plasma. It is the radial projection of the [perturbed plasma
magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field). The right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame has $R$ as major radius, $\phi$ as toroidal
angle, and $Z$ as vertical height.

The plasma-response component is defined by

$$
\delta B_{R,\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $\delta B_{R,\mathrm{pl}}$ is the radial component,
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response magnetic
perturbation, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$
is the cylindrical major-radius unit vector. For a Fourier-resolved
eigenfunction, the projection applies to the specified complex harmonic
coefficient.

Here radial means the cylindrical $R$ direction, not the normal to an
equilibrium magnetic flux surface. The component excludes the equilibrium
field and any separately represented externally imposed vacuum perturbation.
Together with the [toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic
field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field), it describes
directional components of the plasma response; its in-phase component is
represented by the [radial perturbed plasma magnetic field real
part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part).

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic perturbation points toward
increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the signed value of the
poloidal magnetic flux function on the H-mode pedestal-top flux surface.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal top is the signed value of the
poloidal magnetic flux function on the H-mode pedestal-top flux surface. The
pedestal top is the core-side top of the steep edge pedestal and may be
identified by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the value can
be represented as the flux through a horizontal disk bounded by a point on
that flux surface:

$$
\psi_\mathrm{ped} = \int_0^{R_\mathrm{ped}} B_Z(R', Z_\mathrm{ped})\,2\pi R'\,dR'
$$

where $\psi_\mathrm{ped}$ denotes this quantity, $(R_\mathrm{ped},
Z_\mathrm{ped})$ is any point on the pedestal-top flux surface with
$R_\mathrm{ped}$ and $Z_\mathrm{ped}$ in meters, $R'$ is the
disk-integration radius in meters, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field
component in tesla. The integral fixes the additive reference to the
zero-radius disk on the toroidal symmetry axis; only differences in $\psi$
are invariant under an added constant.

This dimensional flux value is related to normalized poloidal magnetic flux
at the pedestal top through the normalization
$(\psi_\mathrm{ped}-\psi_0)/(\psi_b-\psi_0)$, where $\psi_0$ is the
[poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic
axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) and $\psi_b$ is the
[poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary). It is not a
radius-like coordinate such as [toroidal flux radius at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top), and it is distinct from
values at the pedestal center or maximum-gradient surface unless those loci
are defined to coincide with the pedestal top.

Sign convention: Positive when $B_Z$ on the horizontal integration disk
points in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: external_resistance_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Additional externally introduced resistance in a poloidal-field coil
circuit, varying with time and added to the winding resistance to form the
effective coil resistance.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the additional lumped ohmic resistance introduced
externally in the circuit of an individual poloidal-field coil. It
represents resistance from added circuit elements such as dynamically
switchable resistors, rather than the coil winding itself.

At a given time, the effective coil resistance is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{eff}} = R_{\mathrm{winding}} + R_{\mathrm{ext}}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the total effective resistance of the coil
circuit, $R_{\mathrm{winding}}$ is the static winding resistance represented
by [resistance of a poloidal-field
coil](name:resistance_of_poloidal_field_coil), and $R_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is
this additional external resistance.

The quantity applies to one poloidal-field coil and is a scalar lumped
circuit property that may vary as the externally added resistance changes.
It excludes the static winding resistance itself and does not denote an
unrelated power-supply or Thevenin resistance. Its additive relationship to
[resistance of a poloidal-field
coil](name:resistance_of_poloidal_field_coil) distinguishes it from the
baseline winding resistance; together they determine the coil circuit's
effective ohmic opposition and resistive voltage drop.

items.name: radial_center_of_mass_velocity
items.description:
Signed major-radius component of plasma flow, equal to the
mass-density-weighted mean of that component over all constituent species.
items.documentation:
The radial center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the
major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
It retains the mass-density weighting of the full barycentric velocity.

The defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},R} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},R}$ is the radial center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the full center-of-mass velocity vector, $s$
indexes constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density, and
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$
points toward increasing major radius $R$, measured from the toroidal
symmetry axis; $\phi$ is the toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The sum includes all species in the plasma mixture, not only ions. This is a
local mass-density-weighted mean, not a particle-number-weighted mean or an
unweighted sum of species velocities. The definition requires nonzero total
mass density.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its toroidal and
vertical components and is distinct from its speed. The major-radius
direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface or
perpendicular to the magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points away
from the toroidal symmetry axis, toward increasing $R$.

items.name: density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Local number density of a specified plasma species or species group
immediately upstream of a divertor-target sheath, with ion charge states
summed and neutral populations excluded unless explicitly named.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local particle count per volume for a selected plasma
species or species group at the plasma-facing side of a divertor target. It
is evaluated immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath, rather than
in the target material or as a quantity integrated over a target surface.

For a selected set of constituent populations, the number density is defined
by:

$$
n_S = \sum_{s \in S} n_s
$$

where $n_S$ is the number density of the selected species or species group,
$S$ is the set of included constituent populations, and $n_s$ is the number
density of constituent population $s$.

The selected population can be free electrons, one ion species, or a named
group of ion species such as deuterium and tritium. For an ion species, $S$
contains its positive atomic charge states and the sum is an unweighted
particle-count sum; for a compound fuel group, it contains the included
isotope ions. Neutral atoms and molecules are excluded unless explicitly
named as part of $S$. The quantity is local to the plasma immediately
upstream of one divertor-target sheath and is neither a target-surface
integral nor an aggregation over multiple targets.

Species-specific instances refine this common definition, including
[electron density at the divertor
target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), [boron density at the
divertor target](name:boron_density_at_divertor_target), and
[deuterium-tritium density at the divertor
target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target). In contrast,
[total ion number density at the plasma
boundary](name:total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary) sums all charged ion
species at a plasma boundary, making it broader in species scope and
distinct in locus.

items.name: wave_electric_field
items.description:
Complex vector phasor of a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric field,
capturing its local amplitude, phase, and polarization as the oscillatory
contribution to the total electric field.
items.documentation:
The wave electric field is the complex vector phasor representing the
oscillatory electromagnetic-wave contribution to the local [electric
field](name:electric_field). It retains the wave amplitude, phase, and
polarization before any spatial projection or spectral mode decomposition.

For a single angular frequency, the physical wave field is defined by

$$
\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},t)=\operatorname{Re}\left\{\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)e^{-i\omega t}\right\}
$$

where $\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex
wave-electric-field phasor, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $t$ is time, and
$\omega$ is angular frequency. Its projections include the [parallel wave
electric field](name:parallel_wave_electric_field) and [vertical wave
electric field](name:vertical_wave_electric_field); its toroidal Fourier
components are represented by the per-toroidal-mode electric field. The
quantity excludes electrostatic and non-wave contributions unless they are
explicitly part of the identified electromagnetic wave.

items.name: momentum_source
items.description:
Directed rate of momentum transfer to or from a plasma population,
represented as a source density resolved by species, internal state, or
spatial direction.
items.documentation:
A momentum source density represents the directed transfer of momentum
caused by physical processes acting on a plasma population or one of its
resolved states. It may retain vector direction or represent a selected
component of the momentum-transfer rate.

The area-normalized source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{p} = \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src}}$ is the momentum transferred by the source
processes, $A$ is the surface over which the source is normalized, and $t$
is time. Concrete variants may resolve a radial component, an internal
state, or an ion charge state, as in [radial momentum
source](name:radial_momentum_source) and [ion charge-state momentum
source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). Population-level quantities
may sum the corresponding state-resolved contributions, as for [ion momentum
source](name:ion_momentum_source).

items.name: total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
total-momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of total bulk-flow
momentum. The transported momentum density is the aggregate total, not an
unspecified or single-population momentum channel.
items.documentation:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients forming the diagonal of the
total-momentum-diffusivity tensor for diffusive transport of total bulk-flow
momentum. This parent fixes the transported channel to total momentum: the
momentum density is the population-summed aggregate of the constituent
bulk-flow momentum densities included in the total-momentum balance, rather
than an unspecified or single-population channel. Each component is a
kinematic diagonal coefficient for one named transport direction, not a full
viscosity tensor.

For component $\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ associated with coordinate $x_i$
along direction $\hat{e}_i$, the diagonal diffusive closure for total
momentum-density component $M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is

$$
\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff,tot}} = -\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\,\frac{\partial M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial x_i}\qquad\text{(no summation over }i\text{)}
$$

where $\Pi_{ij}^{\mathrm{diff,tot}}$ is the diffusive flux in direction
$\hat{e}_i$ of the $j$ component of total bulk-flow momentum,
$\chi_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the directional total momentum diffusion
coefficient, $M_j^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the $j$ component of total bulk-flow
momentum density, $x_i$ is distance along $\hat{e}_i$, $i$ indexes the named
transport direction, and $j$ indexes the momentum component. The minus sign
defines the down-gradient diffusive contribution for a positive coefficient.

The component basis must be explicit. A radial component is the $\hat{R}$
projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius measured from
the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed
from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height; a toroidal component is
the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the same frame. Poloidal, parallel,
perpendicular-to-magnetic-field, and flux-surface-normal components are
separate named projections; flux-surface-normal is oriented toward
increasing flux label.

This name is the total-momentum specialization of the [momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and is the semantic parent
of direction-qualified components such as the [poloidal total momentum
diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).
It is distinct from species- or population-qualified coefficients such as
the [ion momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) and [neutral momentum
diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), and it
is not the arithmetic sum of those coefficients; it relates the diffusive
flux of aggregate total momentum to the gradient of aggregate total momentum
density.

items.name: vertical_neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis of the effective E×B
drift velocity assigned to a neutral species in one internal state.
items.documentation:
The vertical component of the [neutral-species internal-state E×B drift
velocity](name:neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
is its signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis. This direction
follows increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

For the assigned ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v^0_{E,Z} = \mathbf{v}^0_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v^0_{E,Z}$ is the effective vertical drift component for the specified
neutral internal state, $\mathbf{v}^0_E$ is its assigned ideal E×B drift
velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
local magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the
symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$. The superscript $0$ labels the neutral
population. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified internal state of one neutral
species; it is neither summed nor averaged over internal states or species.
It denotes an effective fluid-velocity contribution, not a direct
electromagnetic guiding-center drift of electrically neutral particles.
Other contributions to neutral motion are excluded, so it is not the total
neutral fluid velocity.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the assigned ideal E×B drift, the vertical
component need not vanish: the symmetry-axis direction is not generally
aligned with the magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the assigned E×B drift velocity has a
component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: parallel_electric_field_at_separatrix
items.description:
Parallel electric field at the separatrix is the electric field projected
along the local magnetic field on the separatrix. It fixes the field-aligned
projection and separatrix locus, while more specific names may add an
aggregation over that locus.
items.documentation:
Parallel electric field at the separatrix is the component of the
electric-field vector along the local magnetic-field direction evaluated on
the separatrix. The separatrix is the magnetic flux surface that separates
the closed-field-line region from the open-field-line edge region.

The field-aligned component at a separatrix point is defined by the
projection:

$$
E_\parallel(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{E}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x}), \qquad \mathbf{x}\in S
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is a spatial point on the separatrix $S$, $\mathbf{E}$ is
the electric-field vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$, and $E_\parallel$
is the resulting parallel electric field.

The scope is limited to the separatrix locus and to the component along
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$; it is not the electric-field magnitude, a component
perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction, or a flux-surface-normal
projection. This parent quantity does not by itself fix a spatial
aggregation over the separatrix; an aggregation qualifier belongs to a more
specific quantity.

The [flux-surface averaged parallel electric field at the
separatrix](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary)
is the flux-surface average of this same $E_\parallel$ over $S$; it differs
only by specifying the aggregation, while the parallel projection and
separatrix evaluation are already part of the present quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field vector has a component in
the direction of the local magnetic-field vector at the separatrix.

items.name: minimum_safety_factor
items.description:
Signed safety-factor value on the closed magnetic flux surface where the
magnitude of field-line winding is smallest, distinct from that surface’s
location.
items.documentation:
The minimum safety factor is the signed field-line winding number evaluated
on the nested closed magnetic flux surface where the magnitude of the safety
factor is smallest. It represents the extremal value of the safety-factor
function within the confined closed-surface domain.

The minimizing value is defined by

$$
q_{\min} = q(\rho_\ast), \qquad \rho_\ast \in \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0 \leq \rho \leq 1} |q(\rho)|
$$

where $q(\rho)$ is the signed [safety factor](name:safety_factor) on the
flux surface labeled by $\rho$, $\rho_\ast$ is the label of a surface at
which the magnitude $|q(\rho)|$ is minimized, and $q_{\min}$ is the signed
value evaluated there. The label $\rho$ is a monotonic flux-surface
coordinate whose endpoints denote the magnetic axis and the last closed flux
surface. In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, $\theta$ is the poloidal
angle and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The extremum is taken over all nested closed magnetic flux surfaces and is
neither a flux-surface average nor a sum. The location-defining quantity is
separate: poloidal magnetic flux at minimum safety factor identifies the
corresponding surface, while this quantity reports only the signed safety
factor. It is also distinct from a safety factor evaluated at a prescribed
locus, such as the magnetic axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angle advance of a magnetic
field line is in the direction of increasing $\phi$ as the poloidal angle
$\theta$ increases.

items.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Parallel flux-limiter coefficient that sets a nonnegative cap on the
field-aligned neutral-particle momentum-flux density for a specified
internal state as a fraction of its collisionless free-streaming bound,
without reversing the signed component.
items.documentation:
Parallel flux-limiter coefficient that applies to neutral particles
occupying a specified internal state is the directional coefficient used to
bound the component of the corresponding neutral internal-state
momentum-flux density parallel to the magnetic field. The internal state may
be an electronic, vibrational, rotational, or other resolved excitation
state, and this scalar coefficient applies to the field-aligned projection
rather than to the poloidal or toroidal projection.

For the parallel component, the limiter defines the admissible cap:

$$
|\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\parallel}| \le \lambda_{\parallel}\,|\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\parallel}|,\qquad 0 \le \lambda_{\parallel} \le 1
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{lim},\parallel}$ is the limited component of the neutral
internal-state momentum-flux density parallel to the magnetic field,
$\Pi_{\mathrm{fs},\parallel}$ is the corresponding collisionless
free-streaming component whose magnitude defines the bound, and
$\lambda_{\parallel}$ is this coefficient.

The inequality is a cap on magnitude rather than an equality for the
realized momentum-flux density. Because $\lambda_{\parallel}$ is
nonnegative, applying the limiter may reduce or bound a signed parallel
momentum-flux component but does not reverse its direction; a nonzero
limited component retains the sign of the underlying field-aligned component
to which the cap is applied. This scalar coefficient is the field-aligned
member of the [neutral internal-state momentum-flux limiter coefficient over
the edge
region](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region)
and is distinct from the
[poloidal](name:poloidal_momentum_neutral_internal_state_flux_limiter_coefficient)
and
[toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
directional members.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_growth_rate
items.description:
Per-toroidal-mode growth rate is the exponential growth or damping rate of a
single linear magnetohydrodynamic eigenmode with a specified toroidal mode
number. It is the imaginary part of the complex eigenfrequency under the
time dependence that makes positive values correspond to increasing
amplitude.
items.documentation:
Per-toroidal-mode growth rate is the exponential rate associated with one
linear magnetohydrodynamic eigenmode at a specified toroidal mode number. It
characterizes the temporal change of that eigenmode's amplitude, separating
unstable growth from damping for the same toroidal harmonic.

For a linear perturbation represented by a toroidal Fourier eigenmode, the
defining convention is

$$
\delta q_n(R,Z,\phi,t) = \tilde{q}_n(R,Z)\exp[i n\phi - i\omega_n t], \qquad \gamma_n = \operatorname{Im}(\omega_n)
$$

where $\delta q_n$ is a perturbation of an MHD field quantity, $\tilde{q}_n$
is its eigenfunction, $n$ is the integer toroidal mode number, $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $t$ is time, $i$ is the
imaginary unit, $\omega_n$ is the complex mode frequency of the eigenmode,
and $\gamma_n$ is the per-toroidal-mode growth rate.

The scope is a single eigenmode within a single toroidal harmonic; there is
no summation, averaging, maximization, or aggregation over toroidal mode
numbers or over distinct eigenbranches. This quantity applies to the linear
perturbation amplitude and excludes nonlinear saturation, mode-coupling
effects, and spectrum-wide instability measures.

This quantity is distinct from mode frequency as an oscillation-rate
quantity and from per-toroidal-mode perturbed energy as an energy-like
quadratic measure of the same toroidal harmonic. For fixed eigenfunction
normalization in the linear regime, a modal amplitude scales as
$\exp(\gamma_n t)$ and a quadratic perturbation measure scales as
$\exp(2\gamma_n t)$.

Sign convention: Positive when the mode amplitude increases exponentially in
time.

items.name: total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower
vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves, summed over lower-region
valves and expressed using the equivalent-electron convention across
injected species.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower
vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves is the lower-region aggregate
equivalent-electron source rate due to gas injection. It counts each
injected neutral atom or molecule by the number of electrons associated with
its neutral composition and sums over all injected species and all
lower-region gas-injection valves.

The multi-species aggregate is defined by:

$$
\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}} = \sum_{v \in \mathrm{lower}} \sum_m E_m\,\dot{N}_{v,m}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}}$ is this total lower gas
source rate, $\dot{N}_{v,m}$ is the neutral gas injection rate of atomic or
molecular species $m$ from lower-region valve $v$, and $E_m = \sum_a
\nu_{a,m} Z_a$ is the equivalent-electron count for one neutral injected
particle of species $m$, with $\nu_{a,m}$ the stoichiometric count of atom
$a$ in species $m$ and $Z_a$ its atomic number.

This quantity is an injected source into the vacuum vessel and excludes
pumping, wall recycling, ionization losses after entry, and gas introduced
outside the lower region. Species-level quantities such as [neon source
rate](name:neon_source_rate) and [propane source
rate](name:propane_source_rate) are individual species contributions under
the same equivalent-electron convention; gas source rate of the vacuum
vessel due to gas injection is the vessel-level source quantity without the
lower-region restriction.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral gas is introduced into the vacuum
vessel through lower-region injection valves.

items.name: total_ion_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
