Total positive-ion number density at the divertor target, summed over all
ionic species and charge states at the entrance to the electrostatic sheath.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local number density of all positive ions in the plasma
immediately adjacent to a divertor target surface. It is the all-ion
aggregate of ion density at the divertor target, rather than a
species-specific or charge-state-resolved density.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_{i,total} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{Z \in \mathcal{Z}_s} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the total ion number density, $s$ indexes
the included ionic species, $Z$ indexes their positive charge states, and
$n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of species $s$ in charge state $Z$. The sums
include all positive-ion populations evaluated at the entrance to the
electrostatic sheath.

Neutral atoms and molecules, as well as free electrons, are excluded. A
density resolved for one charge state is represented separately by [ion
charge state density](name:ion_charge_state_density).

items.name: counter_passing_torque_density
items.description:
Torque density for counter-passing particles is the net angular-momentum
transfer rate to that orbit class per unit volume, retaining the complete
torque-vector direction.
items.documentation:
Torque density for counter-passing particles is the net angular-momentum
transfer rate to the counter-passing population per unit volume. It retains
the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a toroidal
component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{cp}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the angular momentum of the
counter-passing population, $\Delta V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.
The subscript $\mathrm{cp}$ identifies the counter-passing orbit class.

This is the counter-passing specialization of [torque
density](name:torque_density). The [toroidal counter-passing torque
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density) is its
major-radius-weighted toroidal projection, while [co-passing torque
density](name:co_passing_torque_density) applies the same vector definition
to the co-passing orbit class. Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, all
applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions are included.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

items.name: toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Signed toroidal bulk-flow velocity of helium-3 ions evaluated at the
magnetic axis and projected along the direction of increasing toroidal
angle.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local bulk-flow component of the helium-3 ion
population at the magnetic axis, rather than the individual thermal speed or
the full velocity vector.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, its density-weighted
charge-state average is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,3\mathrm{He}}=\left[\frac{\sum_q n_{3\mathrm{He},q}\,\mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{He},q}}{\sum_q n_{3\mathrm{He},q}}\right]_{\mathrm{axis}}\!\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes helium-3 ionic charge states, $n_{3\mathrm{He},q}$ is the
corresponding ion number density, $\mathbf{v}_{3\mathrm{He},q}$ is its fluid
velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle. Neutral helium-3 is excluded. The
species-specific quantity complements the all-ion [toroidal ion
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), while [toroidal helium-3 velocity at
pedestal top](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_pedestal_top) uses a
different radial locus.

Sign convention: Positive when the helium-3 ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit
volume to fast electrons through Coulomb collisions involving the
counter-passing particle distribution.
items.documentation:
Toroidal counter-passing fast-electron collisional torque density is the
flux-surface-averaged angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to
fast electrons through Coulomb collisions involving the counter-passing
particle distribution. It is a component-resolved specialization of [torque
density](name:torque_density).

Its relation to the local collisional torque-density vector is

$$
\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{cp,coll}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp,coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi} \right\rangle
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,e,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ denotes this averaged toroidal
component, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the [counter-passing
fast-electron collisional torque-density
vector](name:counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The
direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. Angle brackets denote the volume-weighted average over an
infinitesimally thin shell between neighboring magnetic flux surfaces.

The counter-passing restriction applies to the contributing particle
distribution; the receiving population is the fast electrons. Co-passing and
trapped contributions are excluded. Torque delivered to bulk thermal
electrons is a distinct quantity, represented by [toroidal counter-passing
thermal-electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
Flux-surface averaging retains torque per volume rather than producing a
volume-integrated torque.

Sign convention: Positive when the flux-surface-averaged collisional torque
received by the fast electrons has a component toward increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$.

items.name: neon_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Neon ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all neon ionization stages.
items.documentation:
Neon density at a limiter is the local number density of neon ions in the
boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The
evaluation point is the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath
entrance at the limiter contact, not the magnetic separatrix, consistent
with the parent [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter).

Unless a charge-state-resolved quantity specifies a particular ionization
stage, this density is summed over all positive neon charge states
($\mathrm{Ne}^{1+}$ through $\mathrm{Ne}^{10+}$):

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z=1}^{10} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the partial number density of neon ions in
charge state $z$.

Neon is introduced as a controlled radiative impurity for power exhaust and
divertor detachment. At the limiter, the local neon density governs
recycling fluxes, charge-exchange with neutral neon, and impurity-driven
edge plasma cooling near the wall. Edge Langmuir probes and vacuum
ultraviolet or extreme ultraviolet spectroscopy provide experimental access
to this quantity.

The neon density in the scrape-off layer at neon-seeded discharges spans
roughly $10^{16}$–$10^{18}$ m$^{-3}$, falling toward the lower end at low
seeding rates and rising with neon puff level. The corresponding quantity
evaluated at the separatrix is
[neon_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:neon_density_at_plasma_boundary);
[xenon_density_at_limiter](name:xenon_density_at_limiter) is the analogous
quantity for xenon impurity injection.

items.name: x_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point
items.description:
Signed Cartesian x coordinate locating the point where a sensor is
mechanically attached to a device component.
items.documentation:
This quantity gives the x-coordinate of a sensor's mechanical attachment
point relative to the origin of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$
frame.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
x_{\rm att} = \mathbf{r}_{\rm att} \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_{\rm att}$ is the position vector of the attachment point
relative to the Cartesian origin and $\hat{x}$ is the unit vector along the
positive x-axis. Together with the [y coordinate of the sensor attachment
point](name:y_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point) and [z coordinate of
the sensor attachment point](name:z_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point),
it specifies the attachment location. A displacement sensor may have two
mechanical attachment points; other sensor types have one.

Sign convention: Positive when the attachment point lies in the positive x
direction from the Cartesian origin.

items.name: resistance_of_vacuum_vessel
items.description:
Lumped ohmic opposition to current flow through a discrete passive-conductor
element of the vacuum vessel.
items.documentation:
Electrical resistance of a discrete passive-conductor element is the
proportionality between the voltage drop across the element and the current
through it, representing irreversible ohmic dissipation.

$$
R = \frac{\Delta V}{I}
$$

where $R$ is the resistance, $\Delta V$ is the potential difference across
the element, and $I$ is the through-current. For an approximately
homogeneous element, resistance is determined by the material resistivity
and the element geometry, as described by [resistivity of the vacuum
vessel](name:resistivity_of_vacuum_vessel) and [resistivity of wall
material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material). This lumped quantity excludes
inductive opposition and represents only the ohmic component; it is distinct
from the total resistance of a closed [passive
loop](name:resistance_of_passive_loop).

items.name: normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Radial flux-surface location of the selected plasma boundary, expressed by
the normalized poloidal flux coordinate. It is the linear normalized
poloidal flux value, increasing from zero at the magnetic axis to one at the
separatrix, of the closed flux surface taken as the plasma boundary;
fixed-boundary equilibrium calculations commonly set it slightly below one
to select a surface just inside the separatrix.
items.documentation:
The normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the plasma boundary is the value
of the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate) on the closed flux
surface selected as the plasma boundary. It is the linear normalized
poloidal flux, labeling the boundary's radial position between the magnetic
axis and the last closed flux surface.

Its value is the poloidal flux difference from the magnetic axis normalized
to the axis-to-separatrix flux difference:

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{N}}^{\mathrm{boundary}} = \frac{\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}{\psi_{\mathrm{sep}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

where $\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic
flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) on the selected plasma-boundary surface,
$\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic
axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis), and
$\psi_{\mathrm{sep}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux at the separatrix (last
closed flux surface).

The label equals zero at the magnetic axis and equals one when the selected
plasma boundary coincides with the separatrix; a value below one selects an
internal closed flux surface. Its defining role is to specify, for
fixed-boundary equilibrium representations, which closed flux surface is
taken as the plasma boundary, commonly a surface just inside the separatrix
so that the boundary remains strictly closed.

This is the linear normalized poloidal flux value itself, not its square
root, and it is a flux-surface label rather than a signed poloidal-flux
value or a geometric minor-radius measure. It is distinct from the
toroidal-flux-based boundary label normalized toroidal flux coordinate at
the plasma boundary, and it belongs to the same locus-valued family as the
normalized poloidal flux coordinate at minimum safety factor and the
[normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
items.description:
Parallel current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the signed
field-aligned projection of electric current generated by the divergence of
perpendicular viscous stress.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the local
field-aligned projection of the electric-current contribution generated by
the divergence of perpendicular viscous stress in a magnetized plasma.

The signed component is defined by:

$$
j_\parallel = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is this parallel component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}}$
is the vector [current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This is a local, mechanism-resolved contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), not the total parallel current density or a
flux-surface average. “Perpendicular” identifies the viscous-stress
mechanism; it does not restrict the resulting current to directions
perpendicular to the magnetic field. The [parallel current density due to
parallel viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity)
uses the same projection but attributes the current to a different
viscous-stress contribution.

The [toroidal current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity) is
another directional projection of the same parent vector, rather than its
field-aligned component.

Sign convention: Positive when the perpendicular-viscosity current
contribution has a projection in the direction of the local magnetic field.
